Trotskyist Fraction – International Strategy (1996-2004)
Trotskyist Fraction – Fourth International (2004-2025)
}} {{Trotskyism}} The '''Current for Permanent Revolution – Fourth International (CPR-FI)''' is a [[political international]] of [[Trotskyism|Trotskyist]] political organizations that claim to adhere to the political legacy of the [[Fourth International]]. Formerly known as the '''Trotskyist Fraction – Fourth International''', it was renamed after its XIV international conference held in São Paulo in December 2025.{{Cite web|url=https://www.leftvoice.org/venezuela-class-struggle-palestine-report-from-the-14th-conference-of-permanent-revolution-cfi/|title=Venezuela, Class Struggle, Palestine: Report from the 14th Conference of Permanent Revolution – CFI|access-date=2025-12-24}} ==History== It has its origin in the expelled Internationalist Bolshevik Faction of the Movement for Socialism (MAS). MAS was the Argentine section of the [[International Workers League (Fourth International)|International Workers League]] (IWL-FI). The Internationalist Bolshevik Faction regarded itself initially as an "external fraction" of the MAS/IWL-FI who had been wrongly expelled, and demanded the overturning of its expulsion. The Internationalist Bolshevik Faction became the [[Socialist Workers' Party (Argentina)|Socialist Workers' Party]] (PTS) in 1988.{{Cite web|url=https://nahuelmoreno.org/wp-content/uploads/2022/10/Balance-Historico-del-MAS.pdf|title=Balance del MAS Período 1987-1992|language=es|access-date=2018-08-07}} In 1989 the ''Partido Obrero Socialista (POS)'' in Mexico, later renamed ''Liga de Trabajadores Socialistas (LTS)'', was also expelled from the IWL-FI.{{cite web|url=https://ceip.org.ar/Alternativa-Socialista|title=Alternativa Socialista|author=CEIP León Trotsky|website=ceip.org.ar|access-date=13 Aug 2024}} The PTS and the POS founded the ''Internationalist Faction of the IWL-FI (IFIWL-FI)'' in 1989.{{cite web|title=Manifiesto de la Fracción Internacionalista de la LIT(CI)|author=PTS and POS|url=https://catalogo.cedinci.org/cgi-bin/koha/opac-detail.pl?biblionumber=67653&shelfbrowse_itemnumber=66743 |website=cedinci.org|access-date=13 Aug 2024}} The Liga Obrera Trotskista in Chile (later renamed Clase contra Clase), which was expelled from the IWL-FI in 1988, joined the IFIWL-FI in 1990.{{Cite newspaper |title=Boletín de Emergencia Nº 1 |newspaper=Estrategia Internacionalista |issue=1 |date=February 1991 |page=1 |url=https://drive.google.com/file/d/1CantdfnfnGdS69m6FAGiH_wmBZWum0GQ/view |publisher=Fracción Internacionalista de la LIT-CI |access-date=2026-10-27 |language=es}}{{cite journal |title=Estrategia Internacional |journal=Estrategia Internacional |issue=6 |date=Winter 1996 |url=https://drive.google.com/file/d/1OOJdqRJQUCQmbzwFoYtW7m8jHKfgkntA/view |publisher=Fracción Trotskista - Estrategia Internacional |access-date=2026-10-27 |language=es}} From 1988 to 1990 the PTS had three splits: first when a number of militants returned to the Argentinian [[Movement for Socialism (Argentina)|Movement for Socialism]] (MAS) party, then when another group of militants sympathized with the British [[Workers Revolutionary Party (Workers Press)|Workers Revolutionary Party (Worker Press)]] and the third when supporters of León Pérez (former member of the International Secretariat of the IWL-FI) decided to follow a mass party perspective (as opposed to a vanguard party). These splits forced the PTS to make a balance and self-criticism. This resulted in a further development. The PTS and the IFIWL-FI questioned the "update" of the [[The Death Agony of Capitalism and the Tasks of the Fourth International|Transitional Program]] that [[Nahuel Moreno]], the leader of the IWL-FI, had made (his so-called theory of "Democratic Revolution").{{cite web | last=Moreno | first=Nahuel | title=The Transitional Program Now, Nahuel Moreno |year=1980 | website=Marxists Internet Archive | url=https://www.marxists.org/archive/moreno/1980/transitional-program/}} The PTS and the IFIWL-FI regarded Moreno's update as an "anti-Trotskyist revision" of [[Leon Trotsky|Leon Trotsky's]] Theory of [[Permanent revolution|Permanent Revolution]].{{Cite web|url=http://www.ft-ci.org/Polemic-with-the-LIT-and-the-theorical-legacy-of-Nahuel-Moreno?lang=en|title=Polemic with the LIT and the theorical legacy of Nahuel Moreno|last=Romano|first=Manolo|website=www.ft-ci.org|language=en|access-date=2018-07-12}} The PTS and the IFIWL-FI broke with Moreno's political tradition/heritage, ideology (termed Morenoism) and tendency (the IWL-FI).{{cite web|url=http://www.ft.org.ar/estrategia/ei3polemica_con_moreno.html|title=Polémica con la LIT y el Legado Teórico de Nahuel Moreno|author=Manolo Romano|website=ft.org.ar|access-date=31 Dec 2013|trans-title=Controversy with the LIT and the Theoretical Legacy of Nahuel Moreno}} The IFIWL-FI was renamed ''Internationalist Faction''. In 1996 the ''Trotskyist Fraction - International Strategy'' (TF - IS) was founded. It admitted the Estratégia Revolucionaria (later renamed Liga Estratégia Revolucionaria - Quarta Internacional), yet another split of the IWL-FI, as its Brazilian section in 1998.{{cite web |url=https://midiaindependente.org/pt/red/2005/08/326339.shtml |title=Votamos construir a Liga Estratégia Revolucionária |access-date=2018-03-21 |website=midiaindependente.org |language=pt |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180322015404/https://midiaindependente.org/pt/red/2005/08/326339.shtml |archive-date=2018-03-22}} The La Liga Obrera Revolucionaria por la Cuarta Internacional (LOR-CI), a split of the [[Revolutionary Workers' Party (Bolivia)]], joined the TF-IS in 1999.{{cite web |url=http://www.geocities.com/lorcuarta/tesisboliviapag1.htm |title=Tesis de la LOR-CI sobre Bolivia. Página 1 |access-date=2018-03-21 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091024164709/http://www.geocities.com/lorcuarta/tesisboliviapag1.htm |archive-date=2009-10-24 |url-status=dead |website=Geocities |language=es}} By 2004 it consisted of the PTS of Argentina, the LTS of Mexico (current name ''MTS''), the LOR-CI of Bolivia,{{Cite web|url=http://www.geocities.com/lorcuarta/tesisboliviapag1.htm|title=Tesis de la LOR-CI sobre Bolivia. Página 1|date=2009-10-24|language=es|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091024164709/http://www.geocities.com/lorcuarta/tesisboliviapag1.htm|archive-date=2009-10-24|url-status=dead|access-date=2018-07-12|quote=Reivindicamos y hacemos nuestro por ello el “Manifiesto Programático” de la FT de febrero de 1998 y las principales elaboraciones planteadas en la revista Estrategia Internacional (especialmente desde marzo de 1998 hasta la fecha) sobre la crisis capitalista internacional y el programa necesario para responder a la misma, la situación de los ex estados obreros deformados y degenerados, las potencialidades y límites de la lucha campesina, la reivindicación de la centralidad revolucionaria del proletariado, así como una posición e intervención común ante la guerra de los Balcanes.}} the Liga Estratégia Revolucionaria - Quarta Internacional, current name ''Movimento Revolucionário de Trabalhadores (MRT)'', of Brazil and the Clase contra Clase, current name ''Partido de Trabajadores Revolucionarios (PTR)'', of Chile as well as some militant sympathizers in Europe. In 2004, in its second international conference, the ''Trotskyist Fraction - International Strategy'' decided to change its name to ''Trotskyist Fraction – Fourth International'' (TF-FI).{{Cite web|url=http://www.ft.org.ar/estrategia/ei21/EI21conferenciaFT.htm|title=Se realizó la Segunda Conferencia de la FT|website=www.ft.org.ar|language=es|access-date=2018-07-12|quote=En este sentido, y dado los avances de los distintos grupos de la FT expresados más arriba, en la conferencia discutimos 'cambiarnos el nombre, llamarnos Fracción Trotskista-Cuarta Internacional (FT-CI) para indicar la relación que hay entre nuestro carácter de tendencia actual y nuestro objetivo de trabajar día a día... hacia la reconstrucción de la Cuarta Internacional'}} Following the economic crisis and demonstrations in several countries, the TF-FI grew in Latin America and Europe, and its manifesto of 2013 called for the formation of a new grouping: An International Movement for a Socialist Revolution – Fourth International.{{Cite web|url=https://www.leftvoice.org/for-a-movement-for-a-revolutionary-socialist-international-the-fourth-international/|title=For a Movement for a Revolutionary Socialist International – The Fourth International|language=en|access-date=2024-08-06}} The manifesto was updated in 2021,{{Cite news|url=https://www.leftvoice.org/the-capitalist-disaster-and-the-struggle-for-an-international-of-socialist-revolution/|title=The Capitalist Disaster and the Struggle for an International of Socialist Revolution|work=Left Voice|access-date=2024-08-06|publisher=Trotskyist Fraction – Fourth International|language=en-US}}{{Cite news|url=http://www.leftvoice.org/The-Battles-of-the-Trotskyist-Fraction|title=The Battles of the Trotskyist Fraction|work=Left Voice|access-date=2018-07-12|publisher=Trotskyist Fraction – Fourth International|language=en-US}} due to new developments in the international arena. In 2005 the TF-FI admitted the Clase Contra Clase (current name Corriente Revolucionaria de Trabajadores y Trabajadoras (CRT)), a split of the [[International Marxist Tendency]], as its Spanish section.{{cite news |url=http://www.laizquierdadiario.com/Nace-la-CRT-un-nuevo-nombre-para-una-nueva-etapa |title=Nace la CRT: un nuevo nombre para una nueva etapa |author=Corriente Revolucionaria de Trabajadores y Trabajadoras (CRT) |work=La Izquierda Diario |access-date=2017-04-29 |language=es}} In addition, the Juventud de Izquierda Revolucionaria from Venezuela, current name Liga de Trabajadores por el Socialismo(LTS), also became a TF-FI section.{{cite web|url=http://www.leftvoice.org/For-a-revolutionary-workers-strategy|title=For a revolutionary workers' strategy|access-date=April 29, 2017|date=March 3, 2007|website=Left Voice|language=en}} ==National sections== The largest full section of CPR-FI is the PTS in Argentina.{{cite web|url=https://www.leftvoice.org/reading-list-on-the-trotskyist-fraction/|title=Reading List on the Trotskyist Fraction|work= Left Voice}} After the [[2023 Argentine general election]] the PTS has four national deputies in the [[National Congress of Argentina]]: [[Nicolás del Caño]],{{cite web|url=https://www.pts.org.ar/Articulos-Nicolas-del-Cano|title=Nicolás del Caño|publisher=Sitio web del PTS}} [[Christian Castillo (politician)|Christian Castillo]],{{cite web|url=https://www.pts.org.ar/Articulo-Christian-Castillo|title=Christian Castillo|publisher=Sitio web del PTS}} [[Myriam Bregman]],{{cite web|url=https://www.pts.org.ar/articulos-myriam-bregman |title=Myriam Bregman|publisher=Sitio web del PTS}} and [[Alejandro Vilca]].{{cite web|url=https://www.pts.org.ar/Articulos-Alejandro-Vilca|title=Alejandro Vilca|publisher=Sitio web del PTS}} The Organización Socialista Revolucionaria (Costa Rica), the Frazione Internazionalista Rivoluzionaria (Italy), and the Corriente Socialista de las y los Trabajadores (Peru) became full sections of CPR-FI after endorsing the CPR-FI manifesto of 2013. In 2022 the [[Révolution Permanente]]{{Cite web|url=https://www.lemonde.fr/politique/article/2023/04/28/a-l-extreme-gauche-revolution-permanente-tente-de-depoussierer-le-trotskisme_6171390_823448.html|title=A l’extrême gauche, Révolution permanente tente de dépoussiérer le trotskisme|publisher=[[Le Monde]]|website=lemonde.fr|access-date=2024-07-20}} in France became a full section of CPR-FI. [[Le Journal du Dimanche]] noted the rising domination of the Révolution Permanente and its youth group, the Le Poing Levé, during the strikes against [[2023 French pension reform strikes|the French pension reform of 2023]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.lejdd.fr/politique/le-poing-leve-lorganisation-etudiante-qui-veut-aider-les-travailleurs-bloquer-le-pays-134877|title=Le Poing Levé, l’organisation étudiante qui veut « aider les travailleurs à bloquer le pays »|publisher=[[Le Journal du Dimanche]]|website=www.lejdd.fr|access-date=2024-08-05}} [[Le Monde]] remarked that the Révolution Permanente's "media visibility" was "disproportionate" to its size during the 2023 protests. According to [[Arrêt sur images]] the website of the Révolution Permanente has become indispensable to striking workers.{{Cite web|url=https://www.arretsurimages.net/articles/les-recettes-de-revolution-permanente-le-media-militant-qui-monte|title=Révolution Permanente, le média militant qui monte|publisher=[[Arrêt sur images]]|website=www.arretsurimages.net|access-date=2024-08-06}} According to [[La Croix (newspaper)| La Croix]], [[Adèle Haenel]], [[Assa Traoré]] and [[Frédéric Lordon]] are supporters of the organization.{{Cite web|url=https://www.la-croix.com/Culture/Adele-Haenel-quest-Revolution-permanente-collectif-dextreme-gauche-lactrice-rejoint-2023-05-10-1201266798|title= Adèle Haenel : qu’est-ce que Révolution permanente, le collectif d’extrême gauche que l’actrice a rejoint?|publisher= [[La Croix (newspaper)| La Croix]]|website=la-croix.com|access-date=2024-08-10}} {| class="wikitable" style="text-align:left;" !colspan="2"|Full sections{{Cite web|url=https://www.laizquierdadiario.com/Sobre-la-XII-Conferencia-de-la-Fraccion-Trotskista-por-la-Cuarta-Internacional-FT-CI|title=Sobre la XII Conferencia de la Fracción Trotskista por la Cuarta Internacional (FT-CI)|website=laizquierdadiario.com|language=es|access-date=2023-11-11}}{{Cite web|url=http://ft-ci.org/spip.php?page=2013_gruposft&lang=es|title=Organizaciones de la FT|website=ft-ci.org|language=es|access-date=2018-07-12}}{{Cite news|url=https://www.laizquierdadiario.com/Apoyemos-la-rebelion-del-pueblo-catalan-y-su-derecho-de-autodeterminacion|title=Apoyemos la rebelión del pueblo catalán y su derecho de autodeterminación|work=La Izquierda Diario|access-date=2018-07-12|language=es-LA}} !Websites |- |[[File:Flag of Argentina.svg|20px]] Argentina |[[Partido de los Trabajadores Socialistas|Socialist Workers' Party]]

{{native name|fr|Forum de São Paulo}} | logo = São Paulo Forum logo.svg | image_border = | image_size = | map = | map_size = | map_caption = | abbreviation = FSP | formation = 1990 (first conference) | extinction = | type = [[Political international]] | languages = [[English language|English]], [[Portuguese language|Portuguese]], [[Spanish language|Spanish]], and [[French language|French]] | status = | purpose = [[South America|South]] and [[Central America]]n network of [[Left-wing politics|left-wing]] [[Political party|political parties]] and [[Political organisation|organisations]] | headquarters = [[São Paulo]], [[Brazil]] | location = | region_served = The Americas | num_members = | leader_title = | leader_name = | main_organ = | parent_organization = | affiliations = | num_staff = | num_volunteers = | budget = | website = | remarks = }} {{Anti-imperialism}} '''São Paulo Forum''' is a conference of [[Left-wing politics|left-wing]] [[Political party|political parties]] and [[Political organisation|organizations]] from the [[Americas]], primarily [[Latin America and the Caribbean]]. It was launched by the [[Workers' Party (Brazil)|Workers' Party]] ({{langx|pt|Partido dos Trabalhadores – PT}}) of [[Brazil]] in 1990 in the city of [[São Paulo]]. The Forum of São Paulo was constituted in 1990, when the Brazilian [[Workers' Party (Brazil)|Workers' Party]] approached other parties of Latin America and the Caribbean to debate the new international scenario after the fall of the [[Berlin Wall]] and rising adoption of some [[economic liberalization]] policies implemented at the time by [[Right-wing politics|right-leaning]] governments in the region. The stated main objective of the conference was to argue for alternatives to [[neoliberalism]].Cf. Carlos Baraibar & José Bayardi: "Foro de San Pablo ¿qué es y cuál es su historia?", 23 August 2000, {{cite web|url=http://www.analitica.com/va/internacionales/noticias/7026753.asp|title=No Se Encontraron Resultados Para Va Internacionales Noticias 7026753 Asp|access-date=2014-02-13|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160309183357/http://www.analitica.com/va/internacionales/noticias/7026753.asp|archive-date=2016-03-09}} The first meeting held in São Paulo in July 1990 was attended by members of 48 parties and organizations from Latin American and the Caribbean. The original name given to the meeting was Meeting of Left and Anti-imperialist Parties and Organizations of Latin America ({{langx|pt|Encontro de Partidos e Organizações de Esquerda e Anti-imperialistas da América Latina}}). Since the 1991 meeting in [[Mexico City]], it started being alternately called Foro de São Paulo in reference to the location of the first meeting.{{cite web|url=http://www2.fpa.org.br/portal/modules/news/article.php?storyid=1727|title=Fundação Perseu Abramo|access-date=16 December 2014|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071120052110/http://www2.fpa.org.br/portal/modules/news/article.php?storyid=1727|archive-date=20 November 2007}} Subsequent meetings have been hosted by many of the parties throughout the region. ==Political stance== According to FSP, more than 100 parties and political organizations participate in its conferences today. Their political positions vary across a wide spectrum, which includes: [[Social democracy|social-democratic]] parties, left-wing [[grassroots]] [[labour movement|labor]] and social movements inspired by the [[Catholic Church]], ethnic and environmentalist groups, [[Anti-imperialism|anti-imperialist]] and nationalist organizations, [[Communist party|communist parties]], and armed [[Guerrilla warfare|guerrilla]] forces. The latter, however, is true only so far as one is willing to think of the [[Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia]] as an actual member of the FSP, when actually the FARC, although never formally banned from the Forum, have been barred from participating in its meetings as early as 2005, when they were refused admittance to that year's meeting of the FSP in São Paulo.[http://www1.folha.uol.com.br/folha/mundo/ult94u407374.shtml Cf. ''Folha de S.Paulo'' May 31, 2005] These groups differ on a range of topics which go from the use of armed force in revolutions to the support of [[representative democracy]]. The [[Communist Party of Cuba]], for example, has adopted a [[One-party state|single-party system]] for decades, while [[Brazil]]'s [[Workers' Party (Brazil)|Workers' Party]] (PT) supports and participates in a [[multi-party system]] of representative democracy. Some parties such as Chile's [[Social Convergence]] advocate for [[radical democracy]], [[participatory democracy]], and [[workplace democracy]] instead of representative democracy as a primary value. These differences grant special relevance to FSP's final declarations, released at the end of each conference, which state the collective position of its members. Ever since FSP's first meeting (1990), the Declaration which was approved expressed the participants' "willingness to renew leftist and socialist thought, to reaffirm its emancipating character, to correct mistaken conceptions, and to overcome all expressions of bureaucratism and all absence of true social and massive democracy." The first Declaration manifests "an active compromise with the validity of human rights, of democracy and of popular sovereignty as strategic values, which place the constant challenge of leftist, socialist and progressive forces renewing their thoughts and actions." At the second conference ([[Mexico]], 1991), FSP expanded its objectives to add the proposal of working toward [[Latin American integration]], an interchange of experiences, the discussion of the political left's differences and searching for consensus in action. The following conferences reinstate the participants' willingness to exchange experiences and develop a dialogue, while at the regional and continental level FSP's influence grows, with some of its members achieving electoral success and their candidates reaching the presidency of many countries. During the early 1990s, the FSP was seen by some as expressing the emergence of a new Latin American leftist paradigm: non-authoritarian, de-militarized and grassroots-friendly.{{cite journal |last=Robinson |first=William I. |title=The Sao Paulo Forum: is there a new Latin American left? |date=December 1992 |journal=Monthly Review |volume=44 |issue=7 |via=[[FindArticles]] |url=http://findarticles.com/p/articles/mi_m1132/is_n7_v44/ai_13272604 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080608061945/http://findarticles.com/p/articles/mi_m1132/is_n7_v44/ai_13272604 |archive-date=June 8, 2008 |url-status=usurped}} As others have noted, however, there is a marked contradiction between the fiery and quasi-revolutionary rhetoric about "[[socialism of the 21st century]]" indulged in sometimes by many FSP's leaders, and the plain fact that the positions of power held by such leaders depend, on most cases, on their holding positions in governments which have emerged through the electoral road.cf. Inés Hayes, "XIV São Paulo Forum: Left parties debate the current historic conjuncture", available at [http://links.org.au/node/495] In a statement made in 2008 in [[Lima]], before a gathering of Peruvian businessmen, however, Brazil's [[President of Brazil|President]] [[Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva|Lula]] would declare, approvingly, that the FSP had "educated" the Left in the understanding of the existence of possibilities of running for elections and gaining power through the democratic way – a declaration that prompted a comment from [[Agence France-Presse|AFP]], reproduced at the [[TV Globo|Rede Globo]] site, to the effect that the hallmark of FSP's activities had been its "very moderate" character.{{cite web|url=http://g1.globo.com/Noticias/Mundo/0,,MUL473012-5602,00.html|title=G1 > Mundo – NOTÍCIAS – Foro de São Paulo ajudou a democratizar esquerda latino-americana, diz Lula|access-date=16 December 2014}} Nevertheless, almost since its inception, the FSP has been the target of criticism from the right in the [[United States]] and Latin America, especially in Brazil, describing it as an organization promoting terrorism and/or a revival of [[communism]],Such as the material found at [http://www.unoamerica.org/unoPAG/libros.php?id=5] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110511095249/http://www.unoamerica.org/unoPAG/libros.php?id=5|date=2011-05-11}} organized by Unoamerica, a coalition of conservative Latin American political groups; see also Luísa Roxo Barja, "A face obscura da política: governo e eleições no Mídia Sem Máscara", ''Aurora-Revista de Arte, Mídia e Política'', no. 4(2009), available at [http://revistas.pucsp.br/index.php/aurora/article/view/4573/3166], retrieved July 20, 2014; and Angelo Kirst Adami, "Hugo Chávez, o ditador : o discurso da revista Veja sobre o presidente da Venezuela", B.Sc Monography IN Communications/Jornalism, UFRGS, 2008, available at [http://www.lume.ufrgs.br/handle/10183/16167], retrieved July 20, 2014 something regarded even by mainstream conservatives as unfounded and "exaggerated to say the least".Cf. [[Kenneth Maxwell]], "Brazil: Lula's Prospects", ''The New York Review of Books'', December 5, 2002, available at [http://www.indopubs.com/cc3.html] The allegedly subversive character of the Foro's activities, however, was revived during the [[2010 Brazilian general election|2010 Brazilian presidential election]] campaign, as the vice-presidential candidate in the [[José Serra]] ticket, [[Antônio Pedro de Siqueira Indio da Costa]], denounced repeatedly the supposed connection, by way of the Foro, between the Brazilian Workers' Party and the FARC.cf., e.g., Venezuela's ''El Universal'', August the 17th. 2010: "FARC causan polémica en debate de candidatos brasileños". Alternatively, the Foro is seen also as more than a simple regular gathering, in that policies that had been advised by it came to be actively implemented later – such as the strengthening of [[Mercosur]], or the setting up of [[Union of South American Nations|Unasur]] – but that the Foro was better understood as a "[[brainstorming]] organization", a "[[Think tank|think-tank]] for politicians".Bruno de Paula Castanho e Silva, "THE SÃO PAULO FORUM AND THE DEVELOPMENT OF LATIN AMERICAN REGIONAL INTEGRATION".Paper presented at the XXIInd World Congress of Political Science, Madrid, 2012. Retrieved Dec 23, 2022 During the fifth meeting (Montevideo, 1995) a dispute arose about the attendance of the [[Free Bolivia Movement|Movimiento Bolivia Libre]], which was charged, in a motion presented by ten parties, led by [[Argentina]]'s [[Workers' Party (Argentina)|Partido Obrero]], of support to the repressive actions of the neoliberal government of [[Gonzalo Sánchez de Lozada]] in Bolivia. The refusal of the motion by the Foro's plenum led to the permanent withdrawal of Partido Obrero from the meeting. Partido Obrero had already declared itself in opposition to the Foro's positions, having previously made public a note in which it protested against the change in the official name of the organization, as "offering evidence of putting, in the place of actual making of common policies, a kind of purely academic workshop, [a sure sign] of conscious depoliticization leading eventually to the cover-up of rightist policies". During the 14th meeting in [[El Salvador]], it was resolved that the Foro should organize a number of subordinate organizations and facilities: an electronic bulletin on the Net, a politic-cultural festival, an electoral observatory and a cadre school.{{Cite web|url=http://www.pt.org.br/portalpt/index.php?option=com_content&task=view&id=6163&Itemid=195|title=Cf. The Foro is interested in achieving peace and in having a negotiated process towards reaching this goal".{{cite web|url=http://www.larepublica.com.uy/politica/312350-foro-de-san-pablo-abre-debates-entre-las-viejas-banderas-y-nuevos-desafios|title=Foro de San Pablo abre debates: entre las viejas banderas y nuevos desafíos|date=23 May 2008|work=LARED21|access-date=16 December 2014}} In the 16th meeting, which opened on 20 August 2009 in [[Mexico City]], the Foro was expected to concentrate discussion on the [[2009 Honduran constitutional crisis]] as well as engaging in efforts to the restoration of the deposed Honduran [[President of Honduras|president]] [[Manuel Zelaya]].{{cite web|url=http://www.vermelho.org.br/noticia.php?id_secao=7&id_noticia=114042|title=Frum de So Paulo discutir sobre Honduras|access-date=16 December 2014}} The Vice president of the [[Senate of the Republic (Mexico)|Mexican Senate]], [[Yeidckol Polevnsky]], has invited the Honduran MP [[Silvia Ayala]], as a member of the [[Democratic Unification Party]] and leader of the manifestations in support of Zelaya held in [[San Pedro Sula]], to attend the meeting[http://www.prensa-latina.cu/index.php?option=com_content&task=view&id=110432&Itemid=1 Cf. [[Left Unity (European Parliament)|Left Unity]] |succeededby = [[The Left in the European Parliament|European United Left–Nordic Green Left]] |englishabbr = EUL |frenchabbr = GUE |formalname = Confederal Group of the European United Left |ideology = [[Socialism]]
[[Communism]] |chairs = [[Alonso José Puerta]] |meps = 28 (19 July 1994) |}} The '''Confederal Group of the European United Left''' was a [[Socialism|socialist]] and [[Communism|communist]] political group with seats in the [[European Parliament]] between 1994 and 1995. ==History== The Confederal Group of the European United Left was formed on 19 July 1994. It consisted of MEPs from the [[United Left (Spain)|United Left]] of Spain (including the [[Communist Party of Spain (main)|Spanish Communist Party]]), the Greek [[Coalition of Left Movements and Ecology|Synaspismós]], the [[French Communist Party]], the [[Portuguese Communist Party]], the [[Communist Party of Greece]], and the [[Communist Refoundation Party]] of Italy. In 1995, the enlargement of the European Union led to the creation of the Nordic Green Left. It consisted of MEPs from the Finnish [[Left Alliance (Finland)|Left Alliance]], the Swedish [[Left Party (Sweden)|Left Party]] and the Danish [[Socialist People's Party (Denmark)|Socialist People's Party]]. The [[Nordic Green Left Alliance]] merged with the Confederal Group of the European United Left on 6 January 1995, and the resultant Group was called the [[European United Left–Nordic Green Left|Confederal Group of the European United Left/Nordic Green Left]]. ==Sources== *[http://www.ena.lu?doc=4327&lang=2 Development of Political Groups in the European wikitext.en:International Meeting of Communist an:
{{Short description|Marxist-Leninist-led communist political international}} {{About|the revivals of these gatherings that have occurred since 1998|the early and ideologically related meetings under the same name|International Meeting of Communist and Workers' Parties (disambiguation)}} {{Use dmy dates|date=September 2022}} {{Infobox recurring event | name = International Meeting of Communist and Workers' Parties | logo = IMCWP logo.png | image = International Meeting of Communist and Workers' Parties.svg | image_caption = Map of countries with at least one party affiliated with the IMCWP | status = Active | frequency = Annual | venue = | inaugurated = {{start date and age|1998}} | organizer = | members = 124 | website = {{URL|http://www.solidnet.org}} }} {{communism sidebar|Organisations}} {{Marxism–Leninism sidebar}} The '''International Meeting of Communist and Workers' Parties''' ('''IMCWP''') is an annual [[Marxist-Leninist]]-led conference attended by [[Communist party|communist]] and [[Labour movement|workers' parties]] from several countries worldwide. It originated in 1998 when the [[Communist Party of Greece]] (KKE) invited communist and workers' parties to participate in an annual conference where [[political party|parties]] could gather to share their experiences and issue a joint declaration.{{cite web |title=International meeting of Communist and Workers Parties, Athens, Greece |url=http://www.cpusa.org/article/international-meeting-of-communist-and-workers-parties-athens-greece/ |website=CPUSA.org |date=8 July 2003 |publisher=Communist Party of the United States of America |access-date=23 November 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191020112115/http://www.cpusa.org/article/international-meeting-of-communist-and-workers-parties-athens-greece/ |archive-date=20 October 2019 |url-status=live}} The IMCWPs bear the same name as the International Meetings of Communist and Workers' Parties that were hosted by the [[Communist Party of the Soviet Union]] (CPSU) throughout the 20th century, for the first time in [[1957 International Meeting of Communist and Workers Parties|1957]]. The parties participating in the IMCWPs can publish materials on their joint website '''SolidNet''', meaning Solidarity Network, which is operated by the KKE.{{cite web |last1=Central Committee of the KKE |first1=International Relations Section |title=The founding, action and dissolution of the Communist International through the prism of the current tasks of the international communist movement |url=https://inter.kke.gr/en/m-article/7c8e6607-bb2b-11f0-b1e1-be037ce642f9/ |website=Communist Party of Greece |access-date=18 August 2026}} SolidNet's declared purpose is "to inform on the activities as well as the ideological and political views of different Communist and Workers' Parties on national and international issues",{{cite web |title=Solid Net |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20001025015426/http://solidnet.org/ |website=Wayback Machine |access-date=18 August 2026}} while it also acts as the official website of the IMCWPs, where the contributions of all the parties of every IMCWP are published.{{cite web |title=IMCWP |url=https://www.solidnet.org/meetings-and-statements/imcwp/ |website=SolidNet |access-date=18 August 2026}} The most recent and 24th IMCWP was held on 7-9 August 2026 in [[Havana]] and hosted by the [[Communist Party of Cuba]] (PCC), under the title "Defending and honouring the legacy of the [[Cuban Revolution]] on the centenary of [[Fidel Castro|Fidel]]’s birth; deepening solidarity with [[Socialist state (communism)|socialist]] [[Cuba]]; strengthening our joint actions; and uniting our forces for peace and against imperialist aggression".{{cite web |title=24th International Meeting of Communist & Workers Parties |url=https://www.solidnet.org/meetings-and-statements/imcwp/24th-international-meeting-of-communist-workers-parties/ |website=SolidNet |access-date=18 August 2026}} The 24th IMCWP was originally scheduled to be held in [[Lebanon]], hosted by the [[Lebanese Communist Party]] (LCP) between 25–27 October 2024,{{Cite web |title=The 24th International Meeting of Communist and Workers' Parties to be held in Beirut in October |url=https://www.idcommunism.com/2024/06/the-24th-international-meeting-of-communist-and-workers-parties-to-be-held-in-beirut-in-october.html |access-date=2024-11-21}} but was postponed due to the [[2024 Israeli invasion of Lebanon|Israeli invasion of Lebanon]]. == Organization == The Working Group (WG) of the International Meetings of Communist and Workers' Parties (IMCWPs) is composed of parties throughout the world. The task of the WG is to prepare and organize the IMCWPs.{{cite web |author=Nota do Gabinete de Imprensa do PCP |title=Sobre a Reunião do Grupo de Trabalho dos Encontros Internacionais de Partidos Comunistas e Operários |url=http://www.pcp.pt/sobre-reuniao-do-grupo-de-trabalho-dos-encontros-internacionais-de-partidos-comunistas-operarios |website=PCP.pt |date=13 May 2013 |access-date=22 November 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170915192939/http://www.pcp.pt/sobre-reuniao-do-grupo-de-trabalho-dos-encontros-internacionais-de-partidos-comunistas-operarios |archive-date=15 September 2017 |url-status=live}}{{cite web |publisher=Solidnet |title=About the Working Group of the International Meeting of Communist and Worker's Parties |url=http://www.solidnet.org/article/About-the-Working-Group-of-the-International-Meeting-of-Communist-and-Workers-Parties/ |access-date=21 November 2019 |archive-date=15 January 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210115230032/http://solidnet.org/article/About-the-Working-Group-of-the-International-Meeting-of-Communist-and-Workers-Parties/ |url-status=live}} The meetings are held annually, with participants from all around the globe. Additionally, there are occasionally extraordinary meetings such as the meeting in [[Damascus]] in September 2009 on "Solidarity with the heroic struggle of the Palestinian people and the other people in Middle East".{{cite web|url= http://www.solidnet.org/article/665152ce-e2ba-11e8-a7f8-42723ed76c54/|title= Working Group, Statement for the Press [En.]|publisher= International Meeting of Communist and Workers' Parties|access-date= 7 April 2021|archive-date= 7 April 2021|archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20210407082804/http://www.solidnet.org/article/665152ce-e2ba-11e8-a7f8-42723ed76c54/|url-status= live}} In December 2009, the communist and workers' parties agreed to the creation of the [[International Communist Review]] (ICR), which is published annually in English, Spanish and Greek and has a website.{{cite web |url= http://www.iccr.gr/ |title= International Communist Review |access-date= 17 June 2015 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20150612103812/http://www.iccr.gr/ |archive-date= 12 June 2015 |url-status= live}} == Participation == {| class="wikitable plainrowheaders sortable" |- ! !! of Vietnam]] }} === 22nd International meeting, 2022 === The 22nd meeting of the Communist and Workers' Parties was held from 27 to 29 October 2022, in Havana, Cuba, with the Communist Party of Cuba as hosting party. The themes for the meeting where "Solidarity with Cuba and all the struggling peoples. United we are stronger in the anti-imperialist struggle, together with social and popular movements, in the face of capitalism and its policies, the threat of fascism and war; in defense of peace, the environment, workers' rights, solidarity and socialism."{{Cite web |title=22nd International Meeting of Communist & Workers Parties |url=http://www.solidnet.org/meetings-and-statements/imcwp/22nd-International-Meeting-of-Communist-Workers-Parties/ |access-date=2023-05-23 |website=solidnet.org |archive-date=17 October 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231017133222/http://www.solidnet.org/meetings-and-statements/imcwp/22nd-International-Meeting-of-Communist-Workers-Parties/ |url-status=live}} The final declaration of the meeting includes; denouncing "the strengthening and expansion of [[NATO]]", "the aggravation of tensions and military conflicts, such as the one in [[Ukraine]]" and "the resurgence of fascism in various parts of the world" and calling for unity to combat the "reemergence of anti-communist, reactionary, ultra-nationalist and fascist forces in various parts of the world".{{Cite web |title=22nd IMCWP, Final Declaration of the 22nd International Meeting of Communist and Workers' Parties |url=http://www.solidnet.org/article/22nd-IMCWP-Final-Declaration-of-the-22nd-International-Meeting-of-Communist-and-Workers-Parties/ |access-date=2023-05-23 |website=solidnet.org |archive-date=4 June 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230604032227/http://www.solidnet.org/article/22nd-IMCWP-Final-Declaration-of-the-22nd-International-Meeting-of-Communist-and-Workers-Parties/ |url-status=live}} Additionally, the meeting called for mobilization of support in favor of the [[Polisario Front]], promoting international solidarity with the [[Bolivarian Republic of Venezuela]], and support for [[Independence movement in Puerto Rico|Puerto Rican independence]]. [[Communist Party of Venezuela]] * [[Communist Party of Vietnam]] === 24th International Meeting, 2026 === The 24th IMCWP was held from 7 to 9 August 2026, in Havana, Cuba, hosted by the PCC. Its title was "Defending and honouring the legacy of the Cuban Revolution on the centenary of Fidel’s birth; deepening solidarity with socialist Cuba; strengthening our joint actions; and uniting our forces for peace and against imperialist aggression". The final speech of the 24th meeting was delivered by the [[President of Cuba|president of the Republic of Cuba]], [[Miguel Díaz-Canel]], who reiterated that Marxism-Leninism "remains fully valid",{{cite web |title=24th IMCWP successfully concluded |url=https://icp.org.tr/news/24th-imcwp-successfully-concluded |website=International Communist Press |access-date=18 August 2026}} despite ongoing [[capitalist]]-inclined economic reforms.[https://www.reuters.com/legal/government/cuba-takes-steps-implement-economic-overhaul-amid-us-pressure-campaign-2026-07-31/ Cuba takes steps to [[Euroscepticism#Soft Euroscepticism|Soft Euroscepticism]] | position = [[Left-wing politics|Left-wing]] | international = | europarl = [[The Left in the European Parliament]] | colours = [[Red]], [[Black]], [[White]], [[Pink]] | headquarters = [[Brussels]] | website = [https://web.archive.org/web/20090814015103/http://www.anticapitalistleft.org/ www.anticapitalistleft.org] (archived) | country = the European Union | abbreviation = EACL }} The '''European Anti-Capitalist Left''' ('''EACL''') was a [[Left-wing politics|left-wing]] [[European political alliance]]. The EACL took part in the Europe against Austerity Conference in 2011.{{cite web|url=http://www.wsws.org/en/articles/2011/10/euro-o11.html|title=European Conference against Austerity seeks to rescue capitalism|date=11 October 2011|access-date=29 July 2013}} In a 2013 [[Rosa Luxemburg Stiftung]] study, the EACL was listed as a European network for the last time.{{cite report |last=Janssen |first=Thilo |title=The Parties of the Left in the Period Leading up to the 2014 European Parliament Election |publisher=Rosa Luxemburg Stiftung |year=2013 |page=12 |url=https://www.rosalux.de/fileadmin/rls_uploads/pdfs/Studien/Studien_The_Parties.pdf |access-date=2026-03-28}} == Ideology == Parties participating in the EACL are united in opposition to [[neo-liberalism]] and [[capitalism]]. The criteria for participation in its conferences are: * A clear foundation in [[anti-capitalism]], with the goal of achieving [[socialism]]. * Recognition of the pluralist nature of the left, with no claim of a monopoly for their own organisation or viewpoint. * Pursuit of common action of the left in general coalitions. * Some degree of representation (in local, regional, or national legislatures) and anchoring in social movements. Despite the last criterion, many organisations involved in the EACL, with the exception of the founding parties, are somewhat marginal groups, often of [[Trotskyism|Trotskyist]] or [[Anti-revisionism (Marxism–Leninism)|Marxist–Leninist anti-revisionist]] persuasion which organize most vigorously through social movements and trade unions, rather than through electoral processes. The EACL emphasises an organizational need to carry out a great deal of [[Extra-parliamentary opposition|extra-parliamentary activism]].{{cite web |url=http://www.uruknet.info/?p=m26124&l=i&size=1&hd=0 |title=Lebanon's victory electrifies Egyptian dissidents: what of the European left? |date=25 August 2006 |access-date=29 July 2013}} == Participants == {{Update section|date=April 2017}} The following table is a list of participants in each meeting. {| class="wikitable sortable" ! The PEL was founded on 8–9 May 2004 in Rome. The elected [[Member of the European Parliament|MEPs]] from member parties of the PEL sit in [[The Left in the European Parliament – GUE/NGL]] group in the [[European Parliament]], though not all PEL members are also members of GUE/NGL. The current president is the Austrian politician [[Walter Baier]]. == History == Before the PEL was founded, most of its members already held annual meetings together, as part of the New European Left Forum (NELF).{{cite news|url=http://www.european-left.org/english/about_the_el/introduction/|title=Some remarks concerning the creation of the Party of the European Left|publisher=Official European Left site|access-date=1 July 2009|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091002092407/http://www.european-left.org/english/about_the_el/introduction|archive-date=2 October 2009}} Several member and observer parties also participated in the more radical [[European Anti-Capitalist Left]]. The Party of European Left (PEL) was formed on 8 and 9 May 2004 in [[Rome]], Italy.{{cite book |last=Hudson |first=Kate |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=LHv_ACE0EekC&pg=PA46 |title=The New European Left: A Socialism for the Twenty-First Century? |publisher=Palgrave Macmillan |year=2012 |isbn=978-1-137-26511-1 |page=46}}{{Citation |last=Hudson |first=Kate |chapter=The Party of the European Left |date=2012 |chapter-url=http://link.springer.com/10.1057/9781137265111_3 |title=The New European Left |pages=46–65 |access-date=2023-04-29 |place=London |publisher=Palgrave Macmillan UK |language=en |doi=10.1057/9781137265111_3 |isbn=978-1-349-32054-7|chapter-url-access=subscription }} The party's first congress took place on 8 October 2005 in [[Athens]], and produced the ''Athens Declaration of the European Left''. Its ideology is based on principles of [[democratic socialism]],{{cite web |last=Nordsieck |first=Wolfram |year=2019 |title=European Union |url=http://www.parties-and-elections.eu/eu.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170608032858/http://www.parties-and-elections.eu/eu.html |archive-date=8 June 2017 |access-date=30 May 2019 |website=Parties and Elections in Europe}}{{cite book |last1=Toplišek |first1=Alen |date=14 March 2019 |title=The Populist Radical Left in Europe |chapter=Chapter 3: Between populism and socialism: Slovenia’s Left party |chapter-url=https://eprints.soas.ac.uk/31138/6/03_Chapter3_Toplisek_rev_kioup-edits.pdf |page=9 |doi=10.4324/9781315180823-4 |s2cid=159164068}} [[socialism]],{{cite book |title=Routledge handbook of European politics |year=2015 |others=José M. Magone |isbn=978-1-317-62836-1 |location=[[Abingdon, Oxfordshire]] |publisher=[[Routledge]] |page=600 |oclc=898475226}} and [[communism]]. It is [[Anti-capitalism|opposed to capitalism]] and consists of parties with wide range of opinions.{{cite book |last=Hudson |first=Kate |title=The new European left: a socialism for the twenty-first century? |year=2012 |publisher=[[Palgrave Macmillan]] |isbn=978-1-137-26511-1 |location=[[Basingstoke]] |oclc=809796420}}{{Rp|page=46}} PEL is also supportive of [[progressivism]].{{Rp|page=50}} It takes a [[Soft Euroscepticism|soft Eurosceptic]] approach towards the European Union,{{cite book |last=Martinelli |first=Alberto |year=2020 |title=European society |publisher=[[Brill Publishers]] |location=[[Leiden]] and [[Boston]] |page=236 |isbn=9789004351776}} and [[Antimilitarism|opposes militarization]] and [[foreign interventionism]].{{Rp|page=53}} PEL opposed the [[Iraq War]] and [[War in Afghanistan (2001–2021)|War in Afghanistan]], and criticised the oppression of [[2009 Iranian presidential election protests]].{{Rp|page=53}} It is also [[List of Anti-NATO parties and organizations|opposed to NATO]] and [[United States military bases]].{{Rp|page=54}} It supports [[Cuba]], and a delegation visited the nation in February 2022.{{Cite web |last=Puig Meneses |first=Yaima |title=Díaz-Canel thanks European Left Party for its longstanding support |url=https://en.granma.cu/cuba/2022-02-16/diaz-canel-thanks-european-left-party-for-its-longstanding-support |website=[[Granma (newspaper)|Granma]]|date=16 February 2022 }} In an interview with the political magazine ''[[Jacobin (magazine)|Jacobin]]'', Walter Baier, the president of PEL, described PEL as part of the "socialist left" and [[Criticism of the European Union|criticised the European Union]], stating that it is [[Neoliberalism|neoliberal]] and "closer to enlightened absolutism than parliamentary democracy".{{Cite web |last=Baltner |first=Adam |date=21 January 2023 |title=If the European Union Doesn't Democratize, It Will Crumble Goldstein]] | leader_title2 = Vice-Chairperson | leader_name2 = [[Grégory Engels]] | leader_title3 = General Secretary | leader_name3 = [[Âlexander Isavnin]] | leader_title4 = Treasurer | leader_name4 = [[Sebastian Krone]] | main_organ = General Assembly | website = [http://www.pp-international.net/ www.pp-international.net] }} {{Pirate Party sidebar|expanded=Parties}} [[File:Pirate Parties Across The World.png|thumb|240px| {{legend|#ff6600|Elected in EU Parliament}} {{legend|#ffaa00|Elected nationally}} {{legend|#aa55ff|Elected locally}} {{legend|#3f48cc|Registered for elections}} {{legend|#7f88ff|Registered in some states}} {{legend|#56cdc1|Unregistered but active}} {{legend|#a0a0a0|Status unknown}}]] [[File:Pirate Parties International Member Parties-March 2026.png|thumb|240px| {{legend|#3f48cc|Ordinary members}} {{legend|#d5adf1|Observer members}}]] '''Pirate Parties International''' ('''PPI''') is an [[Political international|international]] [[Nonprofit organization|non-profit]] and [[non-governmental organization]] with headquarters in [[Brussels]], [[Belgium]].{{cite web |url = http://www.presseurop.eu/en/content/news-brief-cover/234921-pirate-international-born |title = The Pirate International is born |publisher = [[Presseurop]] |date = 2010-04-20 |access-date = 2010-05-17 |archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20110102054618/http://www.presseurop.eu/en/content/news-brief-cover/234921-pirate-international-born |archive-date = 2011-01-02 |url-status = dead }} Formed in 2010, it serves as a worldwide organization for [[Pirate Party|Pirate Parties]], currently representing 39 members from 36 countries across [[Europe]], the [[Americas]], [[Asia]], [[Africa]] and [[Australasia]]. The '''Pirate Parties''' are political incarnations of the [[freedom of expression]] movement, trying to achieve their goals by means of the established [[political system]] rather than solely through [[activism]]. In 2017, PPI was granted special [[consultative status]] to the [[United Nations Economic and Social Council]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.un.org/press/en/2017/ecosoc6843.doc.htm|title=Non-Governmental Organizations Committee Recommends Economic and Social Council Grant Special Status to 14 Entities, Postpones Action on 53 Others | Meetings Coverage and Press Releases}} ==Aims== The PPI statutes{{cite web | title = Pirate Parties International Statutes | url = http://int.piratenpartei.de/wiki/images/a/a6/Statutes_of_the_Pirate_Parties_International.pdf | access-date = 2010-10-07 | date = 2010-04-18 | publisher = Pirate Parties International | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20190224115756/http://int.piratenpartei.de/wiki/images/a/a6/Statutes_of_the_Pirate_Parties_International.pdf | archive-date = 2019-02-24 | url-status = dead }} give its purposes as:
''to help establish, to support and promote, and to maintain communication and co-operation between pirate parties around the world.''
The PPI advocate on the international level for the promotion of goals its members share such as protection of human rights and fundamental freedoms in the digital age, consumer and authors' rights-oriented reform of copyright and related rights, support of information privacy, transparency, and free access to information. The name "Pirates" itself is a reappropriation of the title that was given to internet users by the representatives of the music and film industry and does not refer to any illegal activity. == History == The first Pirate Party was the Swedish [[Pirate Party (Sweden)|Piratpartiet]], founded on 1 January 2006. Other parties and groups were formed in [[Pirate Party of Austria|Austria]], [[Pirate Party of Canada|Canada]], [[Pirate Party (Denmark)|Denmark]], [[Pirate Party (Finland)|Finland]], [[Pirate Party Germany|Germany]], [[Pirate Party (Ireland)|Ireland]], [[Pirate Party (Netherlands)|the Netherlands]], [[Polish Pirate Party|Poland]], and [[Pirate Party (Spain)|Spain]]. In 2007, representatives of these parties met in [[Vienna]], [[Austria]] to form an alliance and plan for the [[2009 European Parliament election]]s.{{cite web |url=http://torrentfreak.com/pirates-gather-at-first-international-pirate-party-conference/ |title=Pirates Gather at First International Pirate Party Conference |author=Ben Jones |publisher=TorrentFreak |date=2007-06-09 |access-date=2010-05-28}} Further conferences were held in 2008 in [[Berlin]] and [[Uppsala]], the latter leading to the "Uppsala Declaration" of a basic platform for the elections.{{cite web |url=http://www.piratpartiet.se/nyheter/european_pirate_platform_2009 |title=The Uppsala Declaration or European Pirate Parties Declaration of a basic platform for the European Parliamentary Election of 2009 |publisher=Piratpartiet |date=2008-07-02 |access-date=2010-05-28 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100908223042/http://www.piratpartiet.se/nyheter/european_pirate_platform_2009 |archive-date=2010-09-08 }} In 2009, the original Pirate Party won 7.1% of the vote{{cite web | url = https://news.bbc.co.uk/1/hi/8089102.stm | title = Swedish pirates capture EU seat | date = 2008-06-08| access-date = 2011-09-26 | work = [[BBC News]] | publisher = [[BBC]]}} in Sweden's [[European Parliament]] elections and won two of Sweden's twenty [[Member of the European Parliament|MEP]] seats, inspired by a surge in membership following the trial and conviction of three members of the ideologically aligned [[The Pirate Bay|Pirate Bay]] a year earlier.{{cite web | url = https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/uk_news/politics/election_2010/8644834.stm | title = Election: Can Pirate Party UK emulate Sweden success? | date = 2010-04-27| access-date = 2011-09-26 | author = Will Smale| work = [[BBC News]] | publisher = [[BBC]]}} On 18 April 2010, the Pirate Parties International was formally founded in Brussels at the PPI Conference from April 16 to 18. === Uppsala Declaration === At the 2009 conference of Pirate Parties International in [[Uppsala]] (Sweden), European Pirate parties agreed on a common declaration of the parties' goals for the upcoming [[2009 European Parliament election|election of the European Parliament]].{{cite web | url = http://www.piratpartiet.se/nyheter/european_pirate_platform_2009 | title = European Pirate Platform 2009 | access-date = 2012-04-05 | publisher = [[Pirate Party (Sweden)]] | url-status = dead | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20100908223042/http://www.piratpartiet.se/nyheter/european_pirate_platform_2009 | archive-date = 2010-09-08 }}{{cite web | url = http://wiki.piratenpartei.de/Uppsala-Deklaration | title = Uppsala-Deklaration | access-date = 2012-04-05 | date = 2010-07-29 | work = Piratenwiki | publisher = [[Pirate Party Germany]] | language = de, en}} Central issues of the declaration are: * reform of [[copyright]], exemption of non-commercial activity from copyright regulation, reduction of the duration of copyright protections; banning of [[Digital rights management|DRM]] technologies, opposition to media or hardware levies; * reform of [[patent law]], particularly stating that patents on life (including patents on seeds and genes) and [[software patent debate|software]] should not be allowed; * strengthening civil rights, transparent government, speedy and fair trial, [[freedom of speech]], and expansion of the right to anonymity in communication. === Prague Declaration === At the conference of Pirate Parties International in [[Prague]] (Czech Republic) in 2012, European Pirate parties agreed to run in the elections to the European Parliament in 2014 with a common program, as well as to establish a [[European political party]]; the [[European Pirate Party]] (PPEU), a [[European political alliance]] was subsequently established in 2014. The declaration[http://ppeu.net/?p=339 The Prague Declaration] has been followed by conferences in [[Potsdam]] and [[Barcelona]] to work on the structure of the legal body to come and the statutes for it. === Hack the Promise Festival Basel 2025 === In 2025, Pirate Parties International board member Schoresch Davoodi presented the keynote '''"Hack the System – At Least a Little"''' at the Hack the Promise Festival in Basel. He reframed the hacker ethos as a democratic practice of precision, openness, and collaboration, arguing that defending freedom today means improving systems rather than destroying them.{{cite web |title=“Hack the System – At Least a Little”: Why Precision Matters in the 21st Century |url=https://piratetimes.info/hack-the-system/ |website=Pirate Times |date=29 October 2025 |access-date=29 October 2025}} === Member Parties=== As of 3 April 2026, the PPI lists the following 28{{cite web |title=Pirate Parties |url=https://pp-international.net/pirate-parties/ |website=Pirate Parties International |publisher=Pirate Parties International |access-date=18 June 2025 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20250618145240/https://pp-international.net/pirate-parties/ |archive-date=2025-06-18}} ordinary members with the voting power of 26 (parties sharing territory split the vote among themselves). It must be noted, however, that the member party list mentions the [[Pirate Party of Australia]] both as an ordinary member and as a former member, without clarifying when the party rejoined, or removing it from the list of ''former ordinary members''. Furthermore, the member party list still mentions the [[Pirate Party (Tunisia)|Pirate Party of Tunisia]] as an ordinary member, although it seems to be defunct. Similarly, it lists the [[United States Pirate Party]] as an ordinary member, although it voted to resign, criticizing the PPI for its stance on the [[Gaza Genocide]] and the [[Israeli occupation of the West Bank]].{{cite web | url=https://uspirates.org/icymi-updates-from-the-2-1-meeting/ | title=ICYMI: Updates from the 2/1 Meeting | date=2 February 2026 |access-date=March 8, 2026|website=United States Pirate Party|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260308185508/https://uspirates.org/icymi-updates-from-the-2-1-meeting/|archive-date=March 8, 2026|url-status=live|quote=The PNC also voted to confirm that we are no longer members of Pirate Party International, voting to leave via unanimous vote. In their statements concerning their resignation and distancing from the PPI, they are also specifically and particularly critical of the [[Pirate Party Germany]] on this matter. == Structure == The PPI is governed by a board, formerly led by two co-chairs,Pirate Parties International Statutes, Article XIII. and since the Warsaw conference of 2015 by a chair and a vice-chair. Policy, governance, and applications for membership are the responsibility of the PPI General Assembly which must convene at least once per year.Pirate Parties International Statutes, Articles IX – XI. By the current rules, board members are elected for a two-year term, half of the board being elected every year. Since the 2019 General Assembly, the Board has 9 members (previously 7). {{Short description|Social democratic and progressive political international}} {{Other uses}} {{Distinguish|Progressive International}} {{Use British English|date=January 2023}} {{Use dmy dates|date=January 2023}} {{Infobox organization | name = Progressive Alliance | image = Progressive Alliance.svg | image_border = | image_size = | caption = Logo | map = | map_size = | map_caption = Light green: Countries with a political party affiliated with the Progressive Alliance
Dark green: Countries with the ruling party affiliated with the Progressive Alliance | abbreviation = PA | formation = {{start date and age|df=yes|2013|05|22}} | extinction = | type = [[Political international]] | purpose = Network of [[Social democracy|social democratic]], [[democratic socialist]] and [[Progressivism|progressive]] political parties and organisations | headquarters = [[Berlin]], Germany | leader_title = Global Coordinator | leader_name = Machris Cabreros | main_organ = Conference of the Progressive Alliance | parent_organization = | affiliations = | num_staff = | num_volunteers = | budget = | website = {{Official URL}} | remarks = }} {{Progressivism sidebar|organizations}} {{Social democracy sidebar|orgs}} The '''Progressive Alliance''' ('''PA''') is a [[political international]] of [[Progressivism|progressive]] and [[Social democracy|social democratic]] political parties and organisations founded on 22 May 2013 in [[Leipzig]], Germany.{{cite book|author=Jean-Jacques Lambin|title=Rethinking the Market Economy: New Challenges, New Ideas, New Opportunities|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=y4CEAwAAQBAJ&pg=PA269|year=2014|publisher=Palgrave Macmillan|isbn=978-1-137-39291-6|page=269}} The alliance was formed as an alternative to the existing [[Socialist International]], of which many of its member parties are former or current members.{{cite book|author=Talbot C. Imlay|title=The Practice of Socialist Internationalism: European Socialists and International Politics, 1914–1960|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=5fU-DwAAQBAJ&pg=PA465|year=2018|publisher=Oxford University Press|isbn=978-0-19-964104-8|page=465}}{{cite book|author=Nathan Gilbert Quimpo|chapter=The Post-war Rise and Decline of the Left|editor1= Toby Carroll|editor2=Shahar Hameiri|editor3=Lee Jones|title=The Political Economy of Southeast Asia: Politics and Uneven Development Under Hyperglobalisation|chapter-url=https://books.google.com/books?id=B1TUDwAAQBAJ&pg=PA150|year=2020|publisher= Springer Nature|isbn=978-3-03-028255-4|page=150}} The Progressive Alliance claims to have 140 participants from around the world. == History == {{Update section|date=April 2026}} The first step towards the creation of the Progressive Alliance was the decision in January 2012 by [[Sigmar Gabriel]], then chairman of the [[Social Democratic Party of Germany]] (SPD), to cancel payment of the SPD's £100,000 yearly membership fee to the [[Socialist International]]. Gabriel had been critical of the Socialist International's admittance and continuing inclusion of undemocratic political movements into the organisation.{{Cite news|url=http://www.spiegel.de/spiegel/vorab/a-810543.html |title=SPD will Sozialistischer Internationale den Geldhahn zudrehen und den Mitgliedsbeitrag nicht zahlen |journal=Der Spiegel |date=22 January 2012 |access-date=23 May 2013}}{{cite web|author=Sigmar Gabriel |url=http://www.fr-online.de/meinung/keine-kumpanei-mit-despoten,1472602,7705378.html |title=Gastbeitrag: Keine Kumpanei mit Despoten |work=Frankfurter Rundschau |language=de |date=3 February 2011 |access-date=23 May 2013}}{{cite book|author=Christian Salm|title=Transnational Socialist Networks in the 1970s: European Community Development Aid and Southern Enlargement|year=2016|publisher=Palgrave Macmillan UK|isbn=978-1-137-55120-7|page=xiv}} An initial Conference of the Progressive Alliance was held in [[Rome]], Italy, on 14–15 December 2012, with representatives of 42 political parties attending.{{cite web|author=Redaktion neues deutschland |url=http://www.neues-deutschland.de/artikel/807483.sozialdemokraten-gruenden-neue-internationale.html |title=16.12.2012: Sozialdemokraten gründen neue Internationale |publisher=NeuesDeutschland |access-date=23 May 2013}}{{cite web |url=http://www.partitodemocratico.it/doc/247636/conferenza-internazionale-dellalleanza-dei-progressisti.htm |title=Progressive Alliance Conference |publisher=Partito Democratico |access-date=23 May 2013 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140419182429/http://www.partitodemocratico.it/doc/247636/conferenza-internazionale-dellalleanza-dei-progressisti.htm |archive-date=19 April 2014 }} They included [[Pier Luigi Bersani]], leader of the [[Democratic Party (Italy)|Democratic Party of Italy]]; [[Harlem Désir]], Chair of the French [[Socialist Party (France)|Socialist Party]]; [[Hermes Binner]], Chair of the [[Socialist Party (Argentina)|Argentine Socialist Party]]; [[Peter Shumlin]], [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] [[governor of Vermont]]; and [[Mustapha Ben Jafar]], Secretary General of the Tunisian [[Democratic Forum for Labour and Liberties]].{{cite web |url=http://www.spd.de/presse/Pressemitteilungen/84228/20121212_gabriel_in_rom.html |title=Sigmar Gabriel in Rom |publisher=Sozialdemokratische Partei Deutschlands (SPD) |language=de |access-date=23 May 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140310171529/http://www.spd.de/presse/Pressemitteilungen/84228/20121212_gabriel_in_rom.html |archive-date=10 March 2014 |url-status=dead }} Also present were representatives of the [[Indian National Congress]], the [[Workers' Party (Brazil)|Workers' Party]] of Brazil, and [[Panhellenic Socialist Movement|PASOK]] of Greece.{{cite web |url=http://www.spd.de/aktuelles/84610/20121217_progressive_alliance.html |title=Progressive Allianz |publisher=Sozialdemokratische Partei Deutschlands (SPD) |language=de |date=22 February 1999 February 2013 |access-date=23 May 2013}} The official foundation of the organisation was held on 22 May 2013 in [[Leipzig]], Germany, on the 150th anniversary of the formation of the [[General German The '''International Communist League (Fourth Internationalist)''' abbreviated as '''ICL(FI)''', earlier known as the '''international Spartacist tendency''' ('''iSt'''), is a [[Trotskyist]] [[List of Trotskyist internationals|international]]. Its largest constituent party is the [[Spartacist League/U.S.|Spartacist League (US)]]. There are smaller sections of the ICL (FI) in [[Mexico]], [[Canada]], [[Ligue trotskyste de France|France]], [[Germany]], [[Ireland]], [[Lega Trotskista d'Italia|Italy]], [[Japan]], [[South Africa]], [[Australia]], [[Greece]] and the [[Spartacist League of Britain|United Kingdom]].

The group originated within the Revolutionary Tendency of the [[Socialist Workers Party (United States)|Socialist Workers Party]] in the United States and, upon its expulsion from the SWP, it named itself Spartacist in 1964 in homage to the original [[Spartacist League]] in [[World War I]] [[German Empire|Germany]], co-led by [[Rosa Luxemburg]] and [[Karl Liebknecht]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Liebknecht and the Spartacists|url=https://www.icl-fi.org/english/wv/974/let-liebknecht.html|work=Workers Vanguard No. 974|publisher=The International Communist League (Fourth Internationalist)|access-date=20 April 2012}}</ref>

==History==

The ICL-FI traces its origins to a factional struggle within the U.S. [[Socialist Workers Party (United States)|Socialist Workers Party]] in the early 1960s. In 1962–63, James Robertson and others organized the [[Revolutionary Tendency (SWP)|Revolutionary Tendency inside the SWP]], which opposed the SWP leadership’s orientation on the [[Cuban Revolution]] and its move toward reunification with the [[Fourth International (post-reunification)|United Secretariat of the Fourth International]] (the so-called "[[Michel Pablo|Pabloites]]"). Initially, the Spartacists aligned with the [[International Committee of the Fourth International]] (ICFI), although relations later broke down.

Following suspensions and expulsions in late 1963–early 1964, they launched the journal ''Spartacist'' in 1964 and formally founded the '''[[Spartacist League/U.S.|Spartacist League (U.S.)]]''' in 1966.<ref name="csudh">{{cite web |title=Guide to the Spartacist League U.S. Collection |url=https://oac.cdlib.org/findaid/ark:/13030/kt4f59q9z3/ |publisher=California State University, Dominguez Hills |access-date=1 September 2025}}</ref>

The international current of the Spartacist League was organized in 1974 as the "international Spartacist tendency", which in 1989 was renamed the "International Communist League (Fourth Internationalist)".<ref name="csudh" /> 

==Publications==
The central theoretical journal of the ICL(FI) is ''Spartacist'' which is published in four languages approximately once a year. Apart from the above the ICL(FI)'s American section, the Spartacist League, operates the [[Prometheus Research Library]] in [[New York City]]. The library has published a number of bulletins and books and houses the tendency's archives and other material on the history of Trotskyism.

In addition to Spartacist the national sections of the ICL(FI) each publish a regular paper of varying regularity. For example, the U.S. group publishes the newspaper ''Workers Vanguard'', which is known for its [[wiktionary:acerbic|acerbic]] running commentary on the activities of other leftist groups, its sarcastic wit, and its obituaries of leftist figures whose lives often are inadequately analyzed and/or memorialized in the mainstream media, recently including [[Bill Epton]], Richard Fraser, [[Robert F. Williams]], and [[Myra Tanner Weiss]]. Since the 1990s ''Workers Vanguard'' has also featured original essays on the history of Marxist and pre-Marxist radical ideas written by long-time member Mark Tishman under the name Joseph Seymour{{Citation needed|date=September 2009}}. From time to time Workers Vanguard also carries features under the rubrics Women and Revolution and Young Spartacus, these being the titles of once separate publications since discontinued.

==Positions==

===Regarding domestic policy===
Since the early 1980s the League and affiliates have also organized mobilizations against [[Nazism|Nazis]] and the [[Ku Klux Klan]]. They were an early campaigner to save [[Mumia Abu-Jamal]] from [[death row]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Mumia Abu-Jamal Is an Innocent Man!|url=https://www.icl-fi.org/english/csdn/oldsite/aff.htm|publisher=The International Communist League (Fourth Internationalist)|access-date=20 April 2012}}</ref> The Spartacist League regards what they term the "struggle for black liberation" as central to [[communist revolution]] in the U.S.; to that end, they promote "revolutionary integrationism"<ref>{{cite web|title=Revolutionary Integrationism: The Road to Black Freedom|url=https://www.icl-fi.org/english/wv/864/fraser.html|publisher=The International Communist League (Fourth Internationalist)}}</ref> and also prominently support the right to bear arms. The party is radically permissive with regards to sexuality and culture, opposing all the laws which prohibit consensual sexual relations. In addition Their British section was for the decriminalization of prostitution, drug use, gambling, pornography, homosexual sex which they regard as "crimes without victims" and are "generally illegal or heavily regulated under capitalist law."<ref>{{cite web|title=On "crimes without victims"|url=https://www.icl-fi.org/english/wh/206/Letter.html|work=Workers Hammer No. 206|publisher=The International Communist League (Fourth Internationalist)|access-date=20 April 2012}}</ref>

===Regarding similar groups===
The League rejects [[left-wing]] political [[coalition]]s and campaigns believing they are [[popular front]]s aimed at providing platforms for bourgeois politicians from the [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic Party]] and the [[Green Party of the United States|U.S. Green Party]], a strategy the SL's ideas abhor.  Instead, the League denounces all support to "[[capitalism|capitalist]] parties", especially the left-wing ones founded through popular front formation, and instead argue for an independent workers' party aiming for [[Political power|state power]].

The Spartacists also devote much attention to [[polemic]]izing against other [[communist]] and [[socialist]] groups. These polemics are usually exceptionally forceful and are often seen by the groups being attacked as unnecessarily disruptive of their activities.{{Citation needed|date=March 2011}} The Spartacist League is also highly critical of groups associated with the [[Fourth International (post-reunification)|reunified Fourth International]], whose politics they characterize as [[Pabloite]].{{Citation needed|date=March 2011}}

In a book entitled ''Death Agony of the Fourth International'', [[Workers Power (Ireland)|Workers Power]] and the [[Irish Workers' Group]] claim the iSt's strategy was/is based on, and they quote from an iSt document, "destroying" other left wing groups. They claim this involves occupying rooms where other left groups are due to have meetings as well as other methods. Furthermore, they argue that the Spartacists, while developing a correct position that the SWP were [[centrist Marxism|centrist]], did not recognise that the Fourth International had degenerated before it split, and therefore were more critical of one section than of the other.

===On Islamic states===
The [[Socialist Workers Party (United States)|Socialist Workers' Party]] supported [[Ayatollah Khomeini]] during the [[Iranian Revolution|Islamic Revolution in Iran]] as "[[anti-imperialism|anti-imperialist]]",<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.marxist.com/why-marxists-not-support-islamic-fundamentalists-1.htm |title=''Why revolutionary Marxists should not support Islamic fundamentalists'' by Maziar Razi |access-date=2009-01-15 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090131032042/http://marxist.com/why-marxists-not-support-islamic-fundamentalists-1.htm |archive-date=2009-01-31 |url-status=dead }}</ref> but the Spartacists gave no support to this. The League was one of the few communist groups other than the [[Workers World Party]] to hail the [[Soviet invasion of Afghanistan]] in 1979 and the occupation that followed. At the time the Spartacists believed it provided an opportunity to extend the gains of the [[October Revolution]] to the [[Afghanistan|Afghan]] people, especially women, in a struggle against the [[misogynistic]] Islamic fundamentalists of the U.S.-backed [[Mujahideen]]. Later, when the U.S. intervention led to the formation of the successive Islamic governments of the [[Mujahideen]] and the [[Taliban]], the League echoed its condemnation of the Islamic Revolution in Iran and denounced these governments as [[theocratic]], capitalist and anti-woman.

===On socialist states===
The League also fought hard in mobilizing to defend the [[Soviet Union]] and [[East Germany]] from what they termed capitalist counterrevolution. Their group in Germany waged a campaign in 1989 calling for [[political revolution (Trotskyism)|political revolution]] against Stalinism and opposition to the capitalist [[German reunification|reunification]]. Today, the Spartacists defend what they see as the remaining [[deformed workers' states]] and have called for the defense of [[North Korea]]'s right to [[nuclear arms]] as a necessary component keeping it free of U.S. military intervention. This is a continuation of their earlier positions on what they consider the deformed workers' states of the [[Republic of Cuba]], the [[Democratic People's Republic of Korea]], [[Socialist Republic of Vietnam]], and the [[People's Republic of China]].  On these countries they continue to call for political revolution against the ruling communist parties while at the same time calling for the defense of these revolutions from imperialism and internal capitalist counter-revolution.

===On lockdowns===

In April 2021 the League issued a Supplement to the Spartacist publication ('Down With the Lockdowns!') in which it announced its opposition to the [[COVID-19 lockdowns]] measures established to reduce the spread of [[COVID-19]], describing these as a "reactionary public health measure" that had caused mass unemployment, and counterposing these measures to 'union control of safety'.<ref>{{cite web |title=Down With the Lockdowns! |url=https://www.icl-fi.org/english/esp/2021-04-lockdown.html |access-date=28 April 2021}}</ref>

==History==

=== Background ===

The first Spartacist League, founded in 1966 with [[James Robertson (Trotskyist)|James Robertson]] as national chairman, developed in the United States from the [[Revolutionary Tendency (SWP)|Revolutionary Tendency]] that had emerged within the [[Socialist Workers Party (United States)|Socialist Workers Party]]. Among their criticisms of the SWP was its embrace of "[[Pabloism]]" and its decision to leave the [[International Committee of the Fourth International]] and join the [[United Secretariat of the Fourth International]]. After its expulsion from the SWP both the Spartacists and the [[Workers League (US)|American Committee for the Fourth International]] were considered affiliates of the ICFI. However, at the 1966 London Conference of the ICFI the positions of the Spartacists were condemned and the ACFI was recognized as the only American ICFI section.<ref>Alexander, Robert ''International Trotskyism: a documented analysis of the world movement'' Durham, Duke University Press 1991 p.552</ref>

=== Establishing an International ===

The American Spartacists remained isolated until [[Bill Logan (Spartacist)|Bill Logan]] formed another Spartacist League in New Zealand in the early 1970s. Logan later expanded the group to become the Spartacist League of Australia and New Zealand. The two groups signed a "Declaration for the organizing of an International Trotskyist Tendency" in July 1974 which proclaimed the combined [[Central Committee|central committees]] an International Executive Committee and an International Secretariat as its executive arm.<ref>Alexander, Robert ''International Trotskyism: a documented analysis of the world movement'' Durham, Duke University Press 1991 p.553</ref>

=== International Spartacist tendency ===

The iSt held its first international conference in England in the summer of 1979. Delegates attended from the United States, Great Britain, Australia, New Zealand, Germany, France and Canada. There were also fraternal delegates from the [[Revolutionary Workers Party (Sri Lanka)|Revolutionary Workers Party of Ceylon]] led by [[Edmund Samarakkody]] and the [[Lega trotskista d'Italia]]. They attempted to recruit both groups to their tendency, but only succeeded with the latter. A new International Executive Committee was also elected.<ref>Alexander, Robert ''International Trotskyism: a documented analysis of the world movement'' Durham, Duke University Press 1991 p.553</ref>

By the 1985 conference of the iSt an "external tendency" had split from the iSt, that would go on to form the [[International Bolshevik Tendency]]. This group had  adherents in the US, Canada and Germany.<ref>Alexander, Robert ''International Trotskyism: a documented analysis of the world movement'' Durham, Duke University Press 1991 p.554</ref> Initially based in the San Francisco Bay area and Toronto the ET was to define itself as a public faction of the SL and sought to be readmitted to the ranks of the parent organization. Said efforts were rebuffed by the SL who have since waged a polemical war with the ET and its successor groups.

The iSt changed its name to the International Communist League (Fourth Internationalist) in 1989 and adopted a new [https://www.icl-fi.org/english/icldop/index.html Declaration of Principles and Some Elements of Program  International Communist League (Fourth Internationalist)] in February 1998.

After the collapse of the USSR, the organization sent its representatives to [[Russia]] and [[Ukraine]] to find like-minded people and create its own sections in the countries. In 1992, a member of the Spartacist League, Marta Philipps, was killed in Moscow. The crime was not solved.<ref>{{cite book |last=Zhvania |first=Dmitry |title=The Way of the Red Guards: a documentary novel |publisher=Издательство «Амфора» |chapter=Chapter 3. The Trotskyist Invasion |date=2006 |isbn=5-367-00269-2}}</ref> The mission itself in Russia continued to operate until 1996, but ended in failure. In 1997, the Customs of Ukraine stopped a group with a large number of leaflets. After that, the group was expelled from Ukraine and the iSt-mission in Ukraine was terminated.{{citation needed|date=November 2023}}

In the summer of 2017, the ICL questioned its past, believing that it had been, in the person of "a number of American cadres" penetrated by "the chauvinist Hydra" since 1974.<ref>Spartacist, English edition, No. 65</ref>

===Later splits===
In 1996, ''[[Workers Vanguard]]'' editor Jan Norden and other founders of the League for the Fourth International were expelled, allegedly for maneuvering with a group from [[Brazil]] involved in bringing court suit against a [[trade union]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.internationalist.org/igbrazila98.html|title = ICL Seeks to Sabotage Defense of Brazilian Trotskyist Workers}}</ref>

The [[Australia]]n section of the Spartacist League, which had previously been involved in IBT events, split again in 2005, with one member leaving to found the Trotskyist Platform.
