[[Parliament of France|Parliament]]; [[Government of France|government]]; [[President of France|president]] }} {{Communism sidebar}} {{Trotskyism|common variants}} '''Lutte ouvrière''' ({{IPA|fr|lyt uvʁijɛʁ}}, {{lit|Workers' Struggle}}; '''LO''') is a [[Trotskyism|Trotskyist]] political party{{Cite news |title=Présentation |url=http://www.lutte-ouvriere.org/qui-sommes-nous/presentation |access-date=2023-03-23 |website=Lutte Ouvrière : Le Portail |language=fr}} in France, named after its weekly paper. [[Arlette Laguiller]] was the party's spokeswoman from 1973 to 2008 and ran in each presidential election during this period. [[Nathalie Arthaud]], her successor, has run for president each time since 2012.{{Cite news |date=2002-04-05 |title=Profile: Arlette Laguiller |url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/europe/1911315.stm |access-date=2024-12-26 |language=en-GB}}{{Cite web |title=French elections: Who else is standing? |url=https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2017/4/13/poutou-arthaud-lassalle-and-other-minor-candidates |access-date=2024-12-26 |website=Al Jazeera |language=en}}{{Cite web |last=Mag |first=Lyon |date=2008-12-09 |title=Lyon Mag |url=https://www.lyonmag.com/article/9385/la-lyonnaise-nathalie-arthaud-nommee-porte-parole-de-lutte-ouvriere |access-date=2024-12-26 |website=Lyon Mag |language=fr-FR}} [[Robert Barcia]] (Hardy) was its founder and central leader. Lutte Ouvrière is a member of the [[Internationalist Communist Union]], an organisation mainly composed of parties upholding [[List of communist ideologies|the Trotskyist interpretation of communism]]. It emphasises workplace activity and has been critical of such recent phenomena as [[alter-globalization]]. The party is against [[reformism]], instead opting for a [[revolutionary socialist]] approach, whilst criticizing past [[communist states]]. == History == === Origins === Its origins lie in the tiny '''Barta group''', a [[Trotskyism|Trotskyist]] organisation founded in 1939 by [[David Korner]] (Barta), also known as '''Union Communiste''' (Communist Union). The group carried out activist efforts in factories throughout [[World War II]] and was instrumental in the [[Renault]] strike of 1947, along with the [[anarcho-syndicalists]]. The group was exhausted by this effort and collapsed in 1950.{{Cite web |last=Prager |first=Rodolphe |date=2008-10-20 |title=KORNER David. Pseudonymes : BARTA, ALBERT, A. MATHIEU |url=https://maitron.fr/korner-david-pseudonymes-barta-albert-a-mathieu/ |url-status=live |access-date=2026-05-11 |website=[[Le Maitron]] |language=fr}} After attempts to revive the Barta group, '''Voix Ouvrière''' was founded in 1956 by [[Robert Barcia]], known as Hardy and the group's pre-eminent leader, and by Pierre Bois, a leading activist in the Renault plant. Effort was made to involve Barta but disputes between him, Hardy and Bois prevented it.{{Cite web |last=Couret |first=Daniel |date=2010-09-21 |title=BARCIA Robert, Félix. Pseudonymes : HARDY, GIRARDOT Roger |url=https://maitron.fr/barcia-robert-felix-pseudonymes-hardy-girardot-roger/ |url-status=live |access-date=2026-05-11 |website=[[Le Maitron]] |language=fr}} VO established itself through the 1960s by producing mass factory bulletins, usually weekly. The [[Communist Party of France]] (PCF) retained its hegemonic position within the workers' movement in France and its members sometimes tried to prevent the distribution of VO bulletins. In part this explains the continued use of semi-clandestine operation within VO and in LO today.{{Citation needed|date=May 2026}} After being banned due to its support of the Students Revolt of [[May 1968 events in France|May '68]], the group became Lutte Ouvrière. === Since the 1970s === An ongoing issue was the possibility and conditions of cooperation with fellow Trotskyist party the [[Revolutionary Communist League (France)|Revolutionary Communist League]] (LCR), the French section of the [[Fourth International (post-reunification)|Fourth International]]. In 1970, LO initiated fusion discussions with the LC (as the LCR was then called). After extensive discussions, the two organisations had agreed the basis for a fused organisation. However, the fusion was not completed.{{Cite book |last=Salles |first=Jean-Paul |url=https://books.openedition.org/pur/21289 |title=La Ligue communiste révolutionnaire (1968-1981): Instrument du Grand Soir ou lieu d'apprentissage ? |publisher=[[Presses Universitaires de Rennes]] |year=2005 |isbn=978-2-7535-3183-3 |location=Rennes |language=fr |chapter=Chapitre II. L’action militante : selon quelles modalités ? |doi=10.4000/books.pur.21297}} In 1976 discussions between the Ligue and Lutte Ouvrière progressed again. The two organisations started to produce a common weekly supplement to their newspapers, common electoral work and other common campaigning. Since then on occasions the two organizations have stood joint candidates at some elections.{{Citation needed|date=May 2026}} LO has made great efforts to stand in elections either on its own or in an alliance with the LCR. As a result, [[Arlette Laguiller]] has become well known to the public as LO's perennial presidential candidate.{{Cite web |last=Lanuque |first=Jean-Guillaume |last2=Nakach |first2=Geneviève |date=2011-07-12 |title=LAGUILLER Arlette, Yvonne, dite Bizet. |url=https://maitron.fr/laguiller-arlette-yvonne-dite-bizet/ |url-status=live |access-date=2026-05-11 |website=[[Le Maitron]] |language=fr}} The early 1970s also saw two breakaways from Lutte Ouvrière. The first such split, in 1974 in Bordeaux, took the name l'Union Ouvrière, but rapidly disintegrated, so much so that when another small split group that developed a year later expected to be able to fuse with l'Union Ouvrière, it found it had already disappeared and were forced to form their own organisation as a consequence. This new group, Combat Communiste, evolved into [[Socialisme International]], an affiliate of the [[International Socialist Tendency]].{{Citation needed|date=May 2026}} Another more recent breakaway developed after Arlette Laguiller's relatively high electoral results in the 1990s and LO's statement that this meant that a new workers' party was a possibility. This statement, as well as a dispute over the personal code members were expected to abide by,{{Citation needed|date=May 2026}} led to the departure of over a hundred members to form the Voix des Travailleurs group.{{Cite journal |last=Beuvain |first=Christian |last2=Salles |first2=Jean-Paul |date=2011-04-02 |title=Trotskysmes en France : chronologie (1928-2009) |url=https://preo.ube.fr/dissidences/index.php?id=144 |journal=Dissidences |language=fr |issue=2 |issn=2118-6057}} This later fused with another smaller group but has more recently joined the [[Revolutionary Communist League (France)|Revolutionary Communist League]] as a recognised faction. In the period up to 2008, a minority faction existed within LO and appeared publicly, although its supporters were segregated in their own cells. Following the very low score of Arlette Laguiller in the first round of the [[2007 French presidential election|April–May 2007 presidential election]] (1,33%, compared to [[2002 French presidential election|5,72% in 2002]]), the party was left with a debt of €1.4 million. According to Michel Rodinson, a party official, the campaign cost was in total €2 million (800,000 of which are paid by the state). The rent of the [[Le Zénith|Zenith]] for meetings in Paris, as well as the December political poster campaign, account for most of the expenses.[http://www.metrofrance.com/fr/article/afp/2007/04/24/070424142028_h2o7rf6h/index.xml Dépenses de campagne: énorme ardoise pour LO, la LCR s'en tire sans déficit]{{dead link|date=January 2018 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}, ''[[Metro International|Metro]]'', 24 April 2007 {{in lang|fr}} [[File:Lutte Ouvriere Mutualite 2008 02 29 n1.jpg|thumb|left|Rally organized by Workers' Struggle (Lutte Ouvrière) on 29 February 2008 at the [[Maison de la Mutualité]] (Paris) for the 2008 town elections.]] In the local elections in 2008, Lutte Ouvrière broke with tradition by joining the [[Socialist Party (France)|Socialist Party]]-led slates by the first round of the elections in a number of towns, preferring this tactic to the more usual option of cooperating with other far left groups to run a joint election campaign. Because an organized minority faction called "L'Étincelle" supported some lists running against lists supported by the party leadership, Lutte Ouvrière suspended the faction from the organization in February 2008; the faction was expelled in September 2008. The faction has agreed to take part in the initial stages of the [[New Anticapitalist Party]] set up by the LCR with others, though this may not be a long-term strategy, with one member explaining it as "foot in both camps" strategy.{{cite web|url= http://www.fifthinternational.org/content/france-lutte-ouvri%C3%A8re-deaf-call-anticapitalist-party|title= France: Lutte Ouvrière deaf to call for anticapitalist party|date = 15 July 2008}}{{cite web|url=http://www.workersliberty.org/story/2008/02/04/lutte-ouvriere-excludes-its-minority|title=Lutte Ouvriere excludes its minority|date=4 February 2008|publisher=[[Workers' Liberty]]}}{{cite web|url=http://www.workersliberty.org/story/2008/09/23/minority-faction-expelled-lutte-ouvriere|title=Minority faction expelled from Lutte Ouvriere|date=23 September 2008|publisher=Workers' Liberty}} Unlike in 2004 and 1999, when it ran common lists with the [[Revolutionary Communist League (France)|Revolutionary Communist League]], LO ran autonomous lists in the [[2009 European Parliament election in France]]. For the [[2022 French legislative election]], LO announced that the party would run its own slate separate from the [[New Ecologic and Social People's Union]], which they believe to be [[reformist]].{{cite web|date=3 May 2022|title=Législatives 2022 : où en sont les négociations des partis de gauche avec La France insoumise ?|url=https://www.francetvinfo.fr/elections/legislatives/legislatives-2022-ou-en-sont-les-negociations-des-partis-de-gauche-avec-la-france-insoumise_5116000.html|access-date=3 May 2022|publisher=France Info|language=fr}} In 2026 the party fielded candidates in more than 240 [[Communes of France|communes]] for the [[2026 French municipal elections|municipal elections]].{{Cite web |title=Elections municipales - les listes Lutte ouvrière - Le camp des travailleurs {{!}} Portail de Lutte Ouvrière |url=https://www.lutte-ouvriere.org/portail/municipales-2026/candidats.html |access-date=2026-03-18 |website=www.lutte-ouvriere.org}} The party gained 24 seats in 18 communes, with the best result in [[Clermont, Oise|Clermont]], where the party won 3 seats (524 votes, 21,48%).{{Cite web |title=Clermont (60157) - Elections Municipales 2026 - Publication des candidatures et des résultats des élections en France |url=https://www.resultats-elections.interieur.gouv.fr/municipales2026/ensemble_geographique/32/60/60157/ |access-date=2026-03-18 |website=www.resultats-elections.interieur.gouv.fr}} ==Fête de Lutte Ouvrière== Another very public activity of LO is their annual [[fête]] which is held in the grounds of a chateau which the organisation purchased for that purpose in 1981. The annual Fête de Lutte Ouvrière has been called "the largest Troskyist rally" by [[France 3]].{{Cite news |last=Ponsy |first=Valentine |date=2017-06-04 |title=Fête de LO : c'est la lutte au château |url=https://france3-regions.franceinfo.fr/paris-ile-de-france/val-d-oise/fete-lo-c-est-lutte-au-chateau-1266711.html |url-status=live |access-date=2026-05-11 |work=[[France 3]] |language=fr}} == Leadership == [[File:Nathalie Arthaud.png|thumb|[[Nathalie Arthaud]]]]The current spokesperson of Lutte Ouvrière is [[Nathalie Arthaud]], a secondary school economics teacher. She has served as the party's spokesperson since 2008{{Cite news |date=2008-12-09 |title=La Lyonnaise Nathalie Arthaud nommée porte-parole de Lutte Ouvrière |url=https://www.lyonmag.com/article/9385/la-lyonnaise-nathalie-arthaud-nommee-porte-parole-de-lutte-ouvriere |url-status=live |access-date=2026-05-11 |work=LyonMag}} and was the party's presidential candidate in 2012, 2017 and 2022. In December 2025, she announced her candidacy for the [[2027 French presidential election|2027 presidential election]].{{Cite news |date=2025-12-08 |title=Présidentielle 2027 : Nathalie Arthaud, porte-parole de Lutte ouvrière, annonce sa candidature |url=https://www.franceinfo.fr/politique/nathalie-arthaud/presidentielle-2027-nathalie-arthaud-porte-parole-de-lutte-ouvriere-annonce-sa-candidature_7665874.html |url-status=live |access-date=2026-05-11 |work=[[France Info]]}} [[Arlette Laguiller]] was the party's spokeswoman from 1973 to 2008 and was its presidential candidate in 1974, 1981, 1988, 1995, 2002 and 2007.[[File:Arlette Laguiller 384133733 b384cfaee6 o d cropped.jpg|thumb|[[Arlette Laguiller]]]] For long, the internal organisations of the party were largely unknown to the general public, the spokeswoman and regular presidential candidate Arlette Laguiller being the only party leader appearing in public. Even to party members, some leaders were known only by cadre names. The party justified such secrecy measures by the possibility that it may have to enter clandestinity, should a highly repressive government take power. For similar reasons, marriages and children were strongly discouraged.{{Citation needed|date=May 2026}} Bernard Seytre, a member of LO for 20 years, confirmed the "iron discipline which rhythms the life of this Trotskyist organisation, whose responsibles [''cadres''] do not have the right to have children, lest they be excluded".{{Cite news |last=Koch |first=François |date=26 December 2002 |title=La chute d'Arlette |url=http://www.lexpress.fr/info/france/dossier/lo/dossier.asp?ida=367858 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070930181348/http://www.lexpress.fr/info/france/dossier/lo/dossier.asp?ida=367858 |archive-date=30 September 2007 |work=[[L'Express (France)|L'Express]] |language=fr}} Lutte Ouvrière was criticised by political opponents in the 2002 presidential campaign as being a [[political cult]], for example by [[Daniel Cohn-Bendit]], his older brother [[Gabriel Cohn-Bendit]], ''[[L'Humanité]]'' and ''[[Libération]]''.{{Cite news|title=Arlette Laguiller n'aime pas le débat |date=11 April 2002 |work=L'Humanité |language=fr |url=http://www.humanite.presse.fr/journal/2002-04-11/2002-04-11-32049 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20050629070722/http://www.humanite.presse.fr/journal/2002-04-11/2002-04-11-32049 |archive-date=29 June 2005 }}[[Daniel Cohn-Bendit]] and his brother Gabriel, [http://www.denistouret.net/constit/Laguiller.html Arlette n'est pas une sainte], ''[[Libération]]'', 4 April 2002 (mirrored) {{in lang|fr}} In part, this strict disciplinary attitude has enabled LO to be a very stable organisation in contrast to the instability that they allege characterises so many other left groups. LO is a difficult organisation to actually join and after becoming a member, individuals are expected to conform to a code of conduct, which is considered old fashioned by some critics. ==Election results== ===Presidential=== {|class="wikitable" |+ [[President of the French Republic]] !rowspan="2"|Election year !rowspan="2"|Candidate !colspan="3"|First round !colspan="3"|Second round !rowspan="2"|Result |- !Votes !% !Rank !Votes !% !Rank |- ![[1974 French presidential election|1974]] |rowspan=6|[[Arlette Laguiller]] |595,247 |2.33 |{{increase}} 5th |colspan=3 {{N/A}} |{{no|Lost}} |- ![[1981 French presidential election|1981]] |668,057 |2.30 |{{decrease}} 6th |colspan=3 {{N/A}} |{{no|Lost}} |- ![[1988 French presidential election|1988]] |606,017 |1.99 |{{decrease}} 8th |colspan=3 {{N/A}} |{{no|Lost}} |- ![[1995 French presidential election|1995]] |1,615,552 |5.30 |{{increase}} 6th |colspan=3 {{N/A}} |{{no|Lost}} |- ![[2002 French presidential election|2002]] |1,630,045 |5.72 |{{increase}} 5th |colspan=3 {{N/A}} |{{no|Lost}} |- ![[2007 French presidential election|2007]] |487,857 |1.33 |{{decrease}} 9th |colspan=3 {{N/A}} |{{no|Lost}} |- ![[2012 French presidential election|2012]] |rowspan=3|[[Nathalie Arthaud]] |202,548 |0.56 |{{steady}} 9th |colspan=3 {{N/A}} |{{no|Lost}} |- ![[2017 French presidential election|2017]] |232,384 |0.64 |{{decrease}} 10th |colspan=3 {{N/A}} |{{no|Lost}} |- ![[2022 French presidential election|2022]] |197,094 |0.56 |{{decrease}} 12th |colspan=3 {{N/A}} |{{no|Lost}} |} ===European Parliament=== {| class="wikitable"style="text-align:center" |- ! 21 (5 May 1999),
13 (13 June 1999) |}} The '''Group of the European Radical Alliance''' ('''ERA''') was a heterogeneous [[political groups of the European Parliament|political group]] with seats in the [[European Parliament]] between 1994 and 1999. It was formed by [[Regionalism (politics)|regionalist]] parties from the former [[Rainbow Group (1984–89)|Rainbow Group]],{{cite book|author=Colin Pilkington|title=Britain in the European Union Today|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=F7uDHZRfZ64C&pg=PA169|year=2001|publisher=Manchester University Press|isbn=978-0-7190-5791-5|page=169}} although its largest and dominant member party was the French [[Radical Party of the Left|Energie Radicale]].{{cite book|author=Julie Smith|title=Europe's Elected Parliament|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=Cih99qAd_uwC&pg=PA92|year=1999|publisher=A&C Black|isbn=978-1-85075-999-7|page=92}}{{cite book|author=Luciano Bardi|chapter=Transnational Trends: The Evolution of the European Party System|editor1=Bernard Steunenberg|editor2=J. J. A. Thomassen|title=The European Parliament: Moving Toward Democracy in the EU|chapter-url=https://books.google.com/books?id=Q30nv4B5icsC&pg=PA215|year=2002|publisher=Rowman & Littlefield|isbn=978-0-7425-0126-3|page=215}} ==History== In 1989 the [[Rainbow Group (1984-1989)|Rainbow Group]] split. The Greens went off to form the [[The Green Group in the European Parliament|Green Group]], whilst the Regionalists stayed in the rump of [[Rainbow Group (1989–94)|Rainbow Group]]. The 1994 elections saw a considerable reduction in Regionalist representation in the Parliament, with only the [[Canarian Coalition|Canary Isles autonomists]], [[Lega Nord]], the [[Scottish National Party]] (SNP) and [[People's Union (Belgium)|People's Union]] (VU) keeping their MEPs. But Lega Nord had been suspended from the [[European Free Alliance]] following its decision to join the coalition Italian government alongside the right-wing [[National Alliance (Italy)|National Alliance]]. Given this reduction in numbers, the weakened EFA were no longer able to maintain their own group. The French [[Radical Party of the Left|Energie Radicale]] were considered [[centrism|centrist]] enough to be possible members of the [[European Liberal Democrat and Reform Party (European Parliament group)|ELDR Group]] (their successors, the [[Radical Party of the Left]], became observers in the [[Alliance of Liberals and Democrats for Europe Party|ELDR Party]] in 2006) but instead they allied themselves with the members of the [[Pannella List|Pannella-Reformers List]] and the rump EFA to form the Group of the European Radical Alliance. The ERA stayed in existence until 1999, when a loss of support forced the [[European Free Alliance]] members of the ERA to rejoin with the Green Group to create the [[Greens–European Free Alliance]] (Greens/EFA) group. {{clr}} ==Member parties on 19 July 1994== {| class="wikitable sortable" |- ! [[Parliament of France|Parliament]]; [[Government of France|government]]; [[President of France|president]] }} {{Communism sidebar}} {{Trotskyism|common variants}} '''Lutte ouvrière''' ({{IPA|fr|lyt uvʁijɛʁ}}, {{lit|Workers' Struggle}}; '''LO''') is a [[Trotskyism|Trotskyist]] political party{{Cite news |title=Présentation |url=http://www.lutte-ouvriere.org/qui-sommes-nous/presentation |access-date=2023-03-23 |website=Lutte Ouvrière : Le Portail |language=fr}} in France, named after its weekly paper. [[Arlette Laguiller]] was the party's spokeswoman from 1973 to 2008 and ran in each presidential election during this period. [[Nathalie Arthaud]], her successor, has run for president each time since 2012.{{Cite news |date=2002-04-05 |title=Profile: Arlette Laguiller |url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/europe/1911315.stm |access-date=2024-12-26 |language=en-GB}}{{Cite web |title=French elections: Who else is standing? |url=https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2017/4/13/poutou-arthaud-lassalle-and-other-minor-candidates |access-date=2024-12-26 |website=Al Jazeera |language=en}}{{Cite web |last=Mag |first=Lyon |date=2008-12-09 |title=Lyon Mag |url=https://www.lyonmag.com/article/9385/la-lyonnaise-nathalie-arthaud-nommee-porte-parole-de-lutte-ouvriere |access-date=2024-12-26 |website=Lyon Mag |language=fr-FR}} [[Robert Barcia]] (Hardy) was its founder and central leader. Lutte Ouvrière is a member of the [[Internationalist Communist Union]], an organisation mainly composed of parties upholding [[List of communist ideologies|the Trotskyist interpretation of communism]]. It emphasises workplace activity and has been critical of such recent phenomena as [[alter-globalization]]. The party is against [[reformism]], instead opting for a [[revolutionary socialist]] approach, whilst criticizing past [[communist states]]. == History == === Origins === Its origins lie in the tiny '''Barta group''', a [[Trotskyism|Trotskyist]] organisation founded in 1939 by [[David Korner]] (Barta), also known as '''Union Communiste''' (Communist Union). The group carried out activist efforts in factories throughout [[World War II]] and was instrumental in the [[Renault]] strike of 1947, along with the [[anarcho-syndicalists]]. The group was exhausted by this effort and collapsed in 1950.{{Cite web |last=Prager |first=Rodolphe |date=2008-10-20 |title=KORNER David. Pseudonymes : BARTA, ALBERT, A. MATHIEU |url=https://maitron.fr/korner-david-pseudonymes-barta-albert-a-mathieu/ |url-status=live |access-date=2026-05-11 |website=[[Le Maitron]] |language=fr}} After attempts to revive the Barta group, '''Voix Ouvrière''' was founded in 1956 by [[Robert Barcia]], known as Hardy and the group's pre-eminent leader, and by Pierre Bois, a leading activist in the Renault plant. Effort was made to involve Barta but disputes between him, Hardy and Bois prevented it.{{Cite web |last=Couret |first=Daniel |date=2010-09-21 |title=BARCIA Robert, Félix. Pseudonymes : HARDY, GIRARDOT Roger |url=https://maitron.fr/barcia-robert-felix-pseudonymes-hardy-girardot-roger/ |url-status=live |access-date=2026-05-11 |website=[[Le Maitron]] |language=fr}} VO established itself through the 1960s by producing mass factory bulletins, usually weekly. The [[Communist Party of France]] (PCF) retained its hegemonic position within the workers' movement in France and its members sometimes tried to prevent the distribution of VO bulletins. In part this explains the continued use of semi-clandestine operation within VO and in LO today.{{Citation needed|date=May 2026}} After being banned due to its support of the Students Revolt of [[May 1968 events in France|May '68]], the group became Lutte Ouvrière. === Since the 1970s === An ongoing issue was the possibility and conditions of cooperation with fellow Trotskyist party the [[Revolutionary Communist League (France)|Revolutionary Communist League]] (LCR), the French section of the [[Fourth International (post-reunification)|Fourth International]]. In 1970, LO initiated fusion discussions with the LC (as the LCR was then called). After extensive discussions, the two organisations had agreed the basis for a fused organisation. However, the fusion was not completed.{{Cite book |last=Salles |first=Jean-Paul |url=https://books.openedition.org/pur/21289 |title=La Ligue communiste révolutionnaire (1968-1981): Instrument du Grand Soir ou lieu d'apprentissage ? |publisher=[[Presses Universitaires de Rennes]] |year=2005 |isbn=978-2-7535-3183-3 |location=Rennes |language=fr |chapter=Chapitre II. L’action militante : selon quelles modalités ? |doi=10.4000/books.pur.21297}} In 1976 discussions between the Ligue and Lutte Ouvrière progressed again. The two organisations started to produce a common weekly supplement to their newspapers, common electoral work and other common campaigning. Since then on occasions the two organizations have stood joint candidates at some elections.{{Citation needed|date=May 2026}} LO has made great efforts to stand in elections either on its own or in an alliance with the LCR. As a result, [[Arlette Laguiller]] has become well known to the public as LO's perennial presidential candidate.{{Cite web |last=Lanuque |first=Jean-Guillaume |last2=Nakach |first2=Geneviève |date=2011-07-12 |title=LAGUILLER Arlette, Yvonne, dite Bizet. |url=https://maitron.fr/laguiller-arlette-yvonne-dite-bizet/ |url-status=live |access-date=2026-05-11 |website=[[Le Maitron]] |language=fr}} The early 1970s also saw two breakaways from Lutte Ouvrière. The first such split, in 1974 in Bordeaux, took the name l'Union Ouvrière, but rapidly disintegrated, so much so that when another small split group that developed a year later expected to be able to fuse with l'Union Ouvrière, it found it had already disappeared and were forced to form their own organisation as a consequence. This new group, Combat Communiste, evolved into [[Socialisme International]], an affiliate of the [[International Socialist Tendency]].{{Citation needed|date=May 2026}} Another more recent breakaway developed after Arlette Laguiller's relatively high electoral results in the 1990s and LO's statement that this meant that a new workers' party was a possibility. This statement, as well as a dispute over the personal code members were expected to abide by,{{Citation needed|date=May 2026}} led to the departure of over a hundred members to form the Voix des Travailleurs group.{{Cite journal |last=Beuvain |first=Christian |last2=Salles |first2=Jean-Paul |date=2011-04-02 |title=Trotskysmes en France : chronologie (1928-2009) |url=https://preo.ube.fr/dissidences/index.php?id=144 |journal=Dissidences |language=fr |issue=2 |issn=2118-6057}} This later fused with another smaller group but has more recently joined the [[Revolutionary Communist League (France)|Revolutionary Communist League]] as a recognised faction. In the period up to 2008, a minority faction existed within LO and appeared publicly, although its supporters were segregated in their own cells. Following the very low score of Arlette Laguiller in the first round of the [[2007 French presidential election|April–May 2007 presidential election]] (1,33%, compared to [[2002 French presidential election|5,72% in 2002]]), the party was left with a debt of €1.4 million. According to Michel Rodinson, a party official, the campaign cost was in total €2 million (800,000 of which are paid by the state). The rent of the [[Le Zénith|Zenith]] for meetings in Paris, as well as the December political poster campaign, account for most of the expenses.[http://www.metrofrance.com/fr/article/afp/2007/04/24/070424142028_h2o7rf6h/index.xml Dépenses de campagne: énorme ardoise pour LO, la LCR s'en tire sans déficit]{{dead link|date=January 2018 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}, ''[[Metro International|Metro]]'', 24 April 2007 {{in lang|fr}} [[File:Lutte Ouvriere Mutualite 2008 02 29 n1.jpg|thumb|left|Rally organized by Workers' Struggle (Lutte Ouvrière) on 29 February 2008 at the [[Maison de la Mutualité]] (Paris) for the 2008 town elections.]] In the local elections in 2008, Lutte Ouvrière broke with tradition by joining the [[Socialist Party (France)|Socialist Party]]-led slates by the first round of the elections in a number of towns, preferring this tactic to the more usual option of cooperating with other far left groups to run a joint election campaign. Because an organized minority faction called "L'Étincelle" supported some lists running against lists supported by the party leadership, Lutte Ouvrière suspended the faction from the organization in February 2008; the faction was expelled in September 2008. The faction has agreed to take part in the initial stages of the [[New Anticapitalist Party]] set up by the LCR with others, though this may not be a long-term strategy, with one member explaining it as "foot in both camps" strategy.{{cite web|url= http://www.fifthinternational.org/content/france-lutte-ouvri%C3%A8re-deaf-call-anticapitalist-party|title= France: Lutte Ouvrière deaf to call for anticapitalist party|date = 15 July 2008}}{{cite web|url=http://www.workersliberty.org/story/2008/02/04/lutte-ouvriere-excludes-its-minority|title=Lutte Ouvriere excludes its minority|date=4 February 2008|publisher=[[Workers' Liberty]]}}{{cite web|url=http://www.workersliberty.org/story/2008/09/23/minority-faction-expelled-lutte-ouvriere|title=Minority faction expelled from Lutte Ouvriere|date=23 September 2008|publisher=Workers' Liberty}} Unlike in 2004 and 1999, when it ran common lists with the [[Revolutionary Communist League (France)|Revolutionary Communist League]], LO ran autonomous lists in the [[2009 European Parliament election in France]]. For the [[2022 French legislative election]], LO announced that the party would run its own slate separate from the [[New Ecologic and Social People's Union]], which they believe to be [[reformist]].{{cite web|date=3 May 2022|title=Législatives 2022 : où en sont les négociations des partis de gauche avec La France insoumise ?|url=https://www.francetvinfo.fr/elections/legislatives/legislatives-2022-ou-en-sont-les-negociations-des-partis-de-gauche-avec-la-france-insoumise_5116000.html|access-date=3 May 2022|publisher=France Info|language=fr}} In 2026 the party fielded candidates in more than 240 [[Communes of France|communes]] for the [[2026 French municipal elections|municipal elections]].{{Cite web |title=Elections municipales - les listes Lutte ouvrière - Le camp des travailleurs {{!}} Portail de Lutte Ouvrière |url=https://www.lutte-ouvriere.org/portail/municipales-2026/candidats.html |access-date=2026-03-18 |website=www.lutte-ouvriere.org}} The party gained 24 seats in 18 communes, with the best result in [[Clermont, Oise|Clermont]], where the party won 3 seats (524 votes, 21,48%).{{Cite web |title=Clermont (60157) - Elections Municipales 2026 - Publication des candidatures et des résultats des élections en France |url=https://www.resultats-elections.interieur.gouv.fr/municipales2026/ensemble_geographique/32/60/60157/ |access-date=2026-03-18 |website=www.resultats-elections.interieur.gouv.fr}} ==Fête de Lutte Ouvrière== Another very public activity of LO is their annual [[fête]] which is held in the grounds of a chateau which the organisation purchased for that purpose in 1981. The annual Fête de Lutte Ouvrière has been called "the largest Troskyist rally" by [[France 3]].{{Cite news |last=Ponsy |first=Valentine |date=2017-06-04 |title=Fête de LO : c'est la lutte au château |url=https://france3-regions.franceinfo.fr/paris-ile-de-france/val-d-oise/fete-lo-c-est-lutte-au-chateau-1266711.html |url-status=live |access-date=2026-05-11 |work=[[France 3]] |language=fr}} == Leadership == [[File:Nathalie Arthaud.png|thumb|[[Nathalie Arthaud]]]]The current spokesperson of Lutte Ouvrière is [[Nathalie Arthaud]], a secondary school economics teacher. She has served as the party's spokesperson since 2008{{Cite news |date=2008-12-09 |title=La Lyonnaise Nathalie Arthaud nommée porte-parole de Lutte Ouvrière |url=https://www.lyonmag.com/article/9385/la-lyonnaise-nathalie-arthaud-nommee-porte-parole-de-lutte-ouvriere |url-status=live |access-date=2026-05-11 |work=LyonMag}} and was the party's presidential candidate in 2012, 2017 and 2022. In December 2025, she announced her candidacy for the [[2027 French presidential election|2027 presidential election]].{{Cite news |date=2025-12-08 |title=Présidentielle 2027 : Nathalie Arthaud, porte-parole de Lutte ouvrière, annonce sa candidature |url=https://www.franceinfo.fr/politique/nathalie-arthaud/presidentielle-2027-nathalie-arthaud-porte-parole-de-lutte-ouvriere-annonce-sa-candidature_7665874.html |url-status=live |access-date=2026-05-11 |work=[[France Info]]}} [[Arlette Laguiller]] was the party's spokeswoman from 1973 to 2008 and was its presidential candidate in 1974, 1981, 1988, 1995, 2002 and 2007.[[File:Arlette Laguiller 384133733 b384cfaee6 o d cropped.jpg|thumb|[[Arlette Laguiller]]]] For long, the internal organisations of the party were largely unknown to the general public, the spokeswoman and regular presidential candidate Arlette Laguiller being the only party leader appearing in public. Even to party members, some leaders were known only by cadre names. The party justified such secrecy measures by the possibility that it may have to enter clandestinity, should a highly repressive government take power. For similar reasons, marriages and children were strongly discouraged.{{Citation needed|date=May 2026}} Bernard Seytre, a member of LO for 20 years, confirmed the "iron discipline which rhythms the life of this Trotskyist organisation, whose responsibles [''cadres''] do not have the right to have children, lest they be excluded".{{Cite news |last=Koch |first=François |date=26 December 2002 |title=La chute d'Arlette |url=http://www.lexpress.fr/info/france/dossier/lo/dossier.asp?ida=367858 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070930181348/http://www.lexpress.fr/info/france/dossier/lo/dossier.asp?ida=367858 |archive-date=30 September 2007 |work=[[L'Express (France)|L'Express]] |language=fr}} Lutte Ouvrière was criticised by political opponents in the 2002 presidential campaign as being a [[political cult]], for example by [[Daniel Cohn-Bendit]], his older brother [[Gabriel Cohn-Bendit]], ''[[L'Humanité]]'' and ''[[Libération]]''.{{Cite news|title=Arlette Laguiller n'aime pas le débat |date=11 April 2002 |work=L'Humanité |language=fr |url=http://www.humanite.presse.fr/journal/2002-04-11/2002-04-11-32049 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20050629070722/http://www.humanite.presse.fr/journal/2002-04-11/2002-04-11-32049 |archive-date=29 June 2005 }}[[Daniel Cohn-Bendit]] and his brother Gabriel, [http://www.denistouret.net/constit/Laguiller.html Arlette n'est pas une sainte], ''[[Libération]]'', 4 April 2002 (mirrored) {{in lang|fr}} In part, this strict disciplinary attitude has enabled LO to be a very stable organisation in contrast to the instability that they allege characterises so many other left groups. LO is a difficult organisation to actually join and after becoming a member, individuals are expected to conform to a code of conduct, which is considered old fashioned by some critics. ==Election results== ===Presidential=== {|class="wikitable" |+ [[President of the French Republic]] !rowspan="2"|Election year !rowspan="2"|Candidate !colspan="3"|First round !colspan="3"|Second round !rowspan="2"|Result |- !Votes !% !Rank !Votes !% !Rank |- ![[1974 French presidential election|1974]] |rowspan=6|[[Arlette Laguiller]] |595,247 |2.33 |{{increase}} 5th |colspan=3 {{N/A}} |{{no|Lost}} |- ![[1981 French presidential election|1981]] |668,057 |2.30 |{{decrease}} 6th |colspan=3 {{N/A}} |{{no|Lost}} |- ![[1988 French presidential election|1988]] |606,017 |1.99 |{{decrease}} 8th |colspan=3 {{N/A}} |{{no|Lost}} |- ![[1995 French presidential election|1995]] |1,615,552 |5.30 |{{increase}} 6th |colspan=3 {{N/A}} |{{no|Lost}} |- ![[2002 French presidential election|2002]] |1,630,045 |5.72 |{{increase}} 5th |colspan=3 {{N/A}} |{{no|Lost}} |- ![[2007 French presidential election|2007]] |487,857 |1.33 |{{decrease}} 9th |colspan=3 {{N/A}} |{{no|Lost}} |- ![[2012 French presidential election|2012]] |rowspan=3|[[Nathalie Arthaud]] |202,548 |0.56 |{{steady}} 9th |colspan=3 {{N/A}} |{{no|Lost}} |- ![[2017 French presidential election|2017]] |232,384 |0.64 |{{decrease}} 10th |colspan=3 {{N/A}} |{{no|Lost}} |- ![[2022 French presidential election|2022]] |197,094 |0.56 |{{decrease}} 12th |colspan=3 {{N/A}} |{{no|Lost}} |} ===European Parliament=== {| class="wikitable"style="text-align:center" |- ! {{Infobox Organisation2}}
Le '''groupe Octobre''' est une troupe de théâtre française d'[[agit-prop]], des [[années 1930]].

== 1932-1936 : Le théâtre ouvrier ==
La troupe de théâtre est issue de la scission de la troupe ''Prémices'' de la [[Fédération du théâtre ouvrier de France]], dont quelques comédiens reprochaient au metteur en scène, [[Roger Legris]], la perte de l'idéal politique. Néanmoins, du {{date|25 avril 1932}}<ref>Arch. [[Centre russe de conservation et d'études des documents en histoire contemporaine|CRCEDHC]], Moscou. Questionnaire rempli par le représentant du collectif, Louis Bonin. Cité dans Haramila Jolly, ''op. cit.'', Mémoire de DEA, p. 11.</ref>, date de sa création, au {{date|30 juin 1936}}, date à laquelle il représenta à la [[Maison de la Mutualité|Mutualité]] son dernier spectacle ''Le Tableau des merveilles'', mis en scène par [[Lou Tchimoukow]], le groupe octobre appartint à la FTOF, née le {{date|25 janvier 1931}} comme section nationale de l'Union internationale du théâtre ouvrier (UITO) et liée au [[Parti communiste français]] (PCF) et la [[Confédération générale du travail unitaire]] (CGTU).

À la suite d'une indication par [[Paul Vaillant-Couturier]] et [[Léon Moussinac]], le groupe Octobre naissant entre en contact avec [[Jacques Prévert]]. À cette époque, celui-ci n'écrivait pas encore beaucoup et ce fut un déclic : il se mit rapidement à écrire à la commande.
Le groupe joua, lors des meetings politiques, dans les rues et dans les usines en grève, entre [[1933]] et [[1936]], de courtes [[pièce de théâtre|pièces]] ou des [[chœur (théâtre)|chœur]]s<ref>{{citation épisode
| titre          =Pas plus grosse qu’une allumette !
| lien épisode   =
| url            =http://media.la-bas.org/mp3/130328/130328.ogg
| série          =Là-bas si j'y suis
| lien série     =Là-bas si j'y suis
| crédits        =[[Raymond Bussières]]
| réseau         =[[Radio France]]
| chaîne         =[[France Inter]]
| diffusion      =28/3/2013
| début          =00:21
| fin            =00:22
| durée          =60:00
}}</ref>, afin de diffuser les idées [[marxisme|marxistes]] auprès du peuple.

Adeptes de l'[[agitprop]], pour un [[théâtre prolétarien]] proche d'[[Erwin Piscator]], Prévert écrivit alors à charge contre l'ordre établi, caricaturant les politiciens et les gros industriels (''La Bataille de Fontenoy'' [[1932]], ''[[Citroën (Jacques Prévert)|Citroën]]''<ref>ou ''Vive la grève''</ref> [[1933]]), ou ridiculisant la bourgeoisie (''La Famille Tuyau de Poêle'', [[1933]]), valorisant les ouvriers (''Vive la presse'', 1932, ou le ''Tableau des merveilles'', joué dans les [[grands magasins]] parisiens en grève en [[1935]]). Face au théâtre bourgeois, il veut favoriser l'émergence d'un théâtre du peuple. Les comédiens jouaient également [[Paul Éluard]] et [[Louis Aragon]].

En {{date|juillet 1935}}, [[Roger Blin]], [[Jean-Louis Barrault (acteur)|Jean-Louis Barrault]] et les frères [[Mouloudji]] rejoignent la troupe, mais celle-ci connait par la suite une période d'inactivité. Elle reprend ses représentations avec l'arrivée au pouvoir du [[Front populaire (France)|Front populaire]] en {{date|mai 1936}}, accompagnant le mouvement de grèves. Une soirée est organisée à la toute jeune Maison de la Mutualité le {{date|1 juillet}} mais ce sera la dernière. Le groupe se sépare sur fond de désaccords politiques (interrogations sur les limites de la gauche au pouvoir, sur la [[guerre d'Espagne]], sur l'Union soviétique, etc) mais ses membres restent en bons termes<ref name=":3">{{Lien web |prénom1=Nicolas |nom1=Beauvillain |titre=Théâtre, jouer pour la classe ouvrière |url=https://www.monde-diplomatique.fr/2023/03/BEAUVILLAIN/65608 |site=[[Le Monde diplomatique]] |date=2023-03-01}}.</ref>.

== Le groupe Octobre et le communisme : histoire d'un mythe==

=== Des travaux contestables ? ===

Les travaux portant sur le groupe Octobre datent de l'après-guerre. Ceux qui évoquent les relations entre Octobre et le communisme apparaissent en 1965. Pour H. Jolly, l'analyse critique des travaux concernant le groupe Octobre fait apparaître la construction progressive d'un mythe. Les relations entre le groupe Octobre et le [[Parti communiste français]] et celui d'Union soviétique ([[PCUS]]) auraient été minimisées voire niées, notamment après l'annonce des « crimes » et « erreurs » de [[Staline]], en {{date|février 1956}}, par le rapport [[Khrouchtchev]], au [[XXe congrès du Parti communiste de l'Union soviétique|{{XXe}} congrès du PCUS]]. C'est en tout cas ce qu'elle déduit de la consultation des archives du [[Centre russe de conservation et d'études des documents en histoire contemporaine|CRCEDHC]] (Centre russe de conservation et d'études des documents en histoire contemporaine), à Moscou<ref>{{Article|langue=fr|auteur=Haramila Jolly|titre=Le groupe Octobre et le communisme : une mémoire reconstruite|périodique=Revue française d'histoire des idées politiques|lieu=Paris|éditeur=[[L'Harmattan]]|numéro=8|date=1998|pages=339-354|issn=1266-7862|hal=01663403}}.</ref>.

Une interprétation différente a été proposée par les universitaires Patrice Allain et Laurence Perrigault<ref name=":0">{{Ouvrage|langue=fr|titre=Jacques Prévert, détonations poétiques|lieu=Paris/14-Condé-en-Normandie|éditeur=Classiques Garnier|collection=Colloques de Cerisy - Littérature|date=2019-05-09|pages totales=357|isbn=978-2-406-08376-4|lire en ligne=https://classiques-garnier.com/jacques-prevert-detonations-poetiques.html|consulté le=2020-04-19}}</ref>{{,}}<ref name=":1">{{Lien web |langue=fr |titre=Le théâtre de Jacques Prévert |url=https://www.musees-normandie.fr/evenement/le-theatre-de-jacques-prevert |site=Réseau des musées de Normandie |consulté le=2020-04-19}}</ref>{{,}}<ref name=":2">{{Lien web |langue=fr |auteur1=Patrice Allain |prénom1=Editions |nom1=Textuel |titre=Editions Textuel - Livre - Photographie, arme de classe |url=http://www.editionstextuel.com/livre/photographie-arme-de-classe |site=www.editionstextuel.com |consulté le=2020-04-19}}</ref>{{,}}<ref>{{Lien web|titre=// Éditions Joseph K. / Temps Noir n°19|url=https://www.editions-josephk.com/TN_21.html|site=www.editions-josephk.com|consulté le=2020-04-19}}</ref>. S'appuyant sur les archives soviétiques et sur les journaux de bord de quelques participants du voyage à Moscou, ils ont montré que les dix encartés du groupe étaient principalement les membres initiaux du groupe Prémices, qui avaient fait appel à Jacques Prévert en {{date|avril 1932}} pour leur écrire un texte sur les élections. Parmi les amis de Prévert qui rejoignirent à partir de cette date le groupe Prémices, bientôt rebaptisé groupe Octobre, pas d'encartés au PC, mais des trotskistes (Yves Allégret, Jacques-André Boiffard, Marcel Jean...) et des anarchistes. La {{3e}} vague d'acteurs à rejoindre le groupe, issue de la bande des arts appliqués (Loris, Grimault, Blin, Janine Jane, etc.) ne témoigna à son tour d'aucune attirance pour le PC : tous signeront d'ailleurs l'Appel à la lutte en {{date|février 1934}} (appel qui excluait l'AEAR{{,}}<ref name=":2" />) et beaucoup participeront à Contre-Attaque.

=== De réelles relations avec le Parti communiste ? ===
Le groupe Prémices était initialement proche du [[Parti communiste français]]. Un an après l'arrivée de Prévert dans la troupe, en {{date|mai 1933}}, le groupe comptait donc 10 membres ayant leur carte au Parti communiste<ref>Arch. [[Centre russe de conservation et d'études des documents en histoire contemporaine|CRCEDHC]], Moscou. Cité dans Haramila Jolly, ''op. cit.'', p. 96.</ref>. Le groupe comptant 26 membres à la même date, cela signifie qu'il y avait environ 40 % de communistes au sein de la troupe de théâtre d'agit-prop, soit guère moins que les Blouses bleues de Bobigny (BBB), nées en 1931, dirigées par Gaston Clamamus et dont [[Raymond Bussières]] disait qu'elles étaient « vraiment communistes à 100 % »<ref>{{Article|langue=fr|auteur=[[Guy Gauthier]]|titre=Il y a trente ans Octobre|périodique=[[La Revue du cinéma (Image et Son)|Image et Son]]|numéro=189|date=décembre 1965|pages=54}}.</ref>. D'autres sont [[Trotskisme|trotskystes]] ou [[Anarchisme|anarchistes]]<ref name=":3" />. Cependant, il faut noter que l'obédience au PC disparaît après le voyage à Moscou, qui refroidit la majorité des membres du groupe<ref name=":0" />{{,}}<ref name=":1" />. Le compte rendu du spectacle donné par la troupe à Moscou regrettait d'ailleurs que le groupe ne suivait pas suffisamment la ligne donnée par le PC et exigeait qu'à leur retour en France tous les membres du groupe suivent des cours de politique{{Référence nécessaire|date=6 avril 2023}}. "Il faut dégager un responsable idéologique." Germinal{{Qui|date=6 avril 2023}} soulignait qu'en France, le spectacle qui avait été présenté par le Groupe Octobre à Moscou avait une thématique anarchiste bien plus forte et qu'il avait été en partie réécrit pour les Olympiades. Moussinac{{Qui|date=6 avril 2023}} mettait toutefois en garde : "Je suis d’accord sur le fait qu’il est nécessaire de prendre des mesures de réorganisation et de formation politique pour restructurer le groupe, mais il faudra le faire avec beaucoup de précautions, sans quoi nous pourrions causer sa perte". De fait, au retour de Moscou, les membres de Prémices encartés au PC quittèrent peu à peu le groupe, tandis que celui-ci accueillait de nouveaux membres non encartés. Les deux dernières représentations du groupe données en 1936 le furent, l'une en l'honneur de [[Trotsky]], l'autre - organisée par le comité [[Anarcho-syndicalisme|anarcho-syndicaliste]] - au profit des combattants de la [[C.N.T|CNT]] et de la [[Fédération anarchiste ibérique|FAI]]<ref>{{Ouvrage|langue=fr|auteur1=Gilles Bounoure|titre=Revue Contretemps n° 42|lieu=Paris|éditeur=|date=juillet 2019|passage="Chez Jacques Prévert, le groupe Octobre"|isbn=|lire en ligne=http://lesdossiers-contretemps.org/2019/07/10/contretemps-n-42-le-medicament-un-bien-commun/}}</ref>.
 
=== Un premier Prix fantasmé ===
Contrairement à ce qu'écrit Michel Fauré dans son ouvrage<ref>Michel Fauré, ''Le Groupe Octobre'', Paris, Bourgeois, 1977, p. 55</ref> et beaucoup d'autres auteurs, le groupe Octobre n'a pas remporté le premier prix de l'Olympiade du théâtre ouvrier de [[Moscou]] qui s'est déroulée à Moscou, en 1933. En effet, comme l'a précisé lui-même Raymond Bussières dans un témoignage antérieur, « il n'y avait pas de premier prix »<ref>Guy Gautier, ''op. cit.'', p. 203</ref> lors de cette Olympiade. Celle-ci devait se terminer par une conférence, sans remise de prix, comme l'atteste le programme de l'Olympiade<ref>Arch. CRCEDHC, Moscou. Cité dans Haramila Jolly, ''op. cit.'', Mémoire de DEA, p. 108</ref>.

== Dissolution du groupe ==

La compagnie fut dissoute, comme la Fédération du théâtre ouvrier de France, après la victoire du [[Front populaire (France)|Front populaire]], sur fond de désaccord des membres quant à la nécessité de s'engager dans les [[Brigades internationales]].
